title.zh: 卷五十八 吳書十三 陸遜傳
title.en: Volume 58: Book of Wu 13 - Biography of Lu Xun
title.raw: 卷五十八 吳書十三 陸遜傳 Volume 58: Book of Wu 13 - Biography of Lu Xun

sentences.zh: 陸遜字伯言，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Xun, courtesy name Boyan, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun, styled Boyan, came from Wu in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 本名議，世江東大族。

translations.literal: His original given name was Yi; for generations his clan had been a great family east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name was Yi, and his lineage ranked among the great houses of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 〈陆氏世颂曰：逊祖纡，字叔盘，敏淑有思学，守城门校尉。

translations.literal: The Lu Clan Epic Praise states: Xun's ancestor Shu, courtesy name Shupan, was quick, virtuous, thoughtful, and fond of learning; he served as Colonel of the City Gates.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Lu Clan Epic Praise, Xun's grandfather Shu, styled Shupan, was clever and cultivated, fond of study, and rose to Colonel of the City Gates.

sentences.zh: 父骏，字季才，淳懿信厚，为邦族所怀，官至九江都尉。〉

translations.literal: His father Jun, courtesy name Jicai, was honest, kindly, trustworthy, and generous; the community cherished him, and he reached the rank of Commandant of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun, styled Jicai, was plain-dealing, trustworthy, and deeply respected by kinsmen and neighbors; his highest office was Commandant of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 遜少孤，隨從祖廬江太守康在官。

translations.literal: Xun was orphaned young and accompanied his grandfather's brother Kang, the Administrator of Lujiang, while Kang held office.
translations.idiomatic: Xun lost his father while still a boy and lived with his great-uncle Kang, who served as Administrator of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 袁術與康有隙，將攻康，康遣遜及親戚還吳。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu bore Kang a grudge and was about to attack him; Kang sent Xun and his relatives back to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu nursed a grievance against Kang and prepared to strike; Kang sent Xun and the rest of the family home to Wu.

sentences.zh: 遜年長於康子績數歲，為之綱紀門戶。

translations.literal: Xun was several years older than Kang's son Ji and managed the household for him.
translations.idiomatic: Several years Kang's son Ji's senior, Xun kept order in the family and ran its affairs.

sentences.zh: 孫權為將軍，遜年二十一。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan was General, Xun was twenty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan had already taken the title of general when Xun turned twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 始仕幕府，歷東西曹令史，出為海昌屯田都尉，並領縣事。

translations.literal: He first entered service in the headquarters staff, served successively as clerk of the eastern and western bureaus, then went out as Colonel of Agricultural Garrison at Haichang and concurrently administered the county.
translations.idiomatic: He began in headquarters as clerk of the eastern and western offices, then was posted Colonel of Agricultural Garrison at Haichang with civil duties over the county.

sentences.zh: 〈陆氏祠堂像赞曰：海昌，今盐官县也。〉

translations.literal: The Lu Clan Shrine Portrait Inscription states: Haichang is today Yanguan County.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription at the Lu ancestral shrine notes that Haichang corresponds to present-day Yanguan County.

sentences.zh: 縣連年亢旱，遜開倉谷以振貧民，勸督農桑，百姓蒙賴。

translations.literal: The county had suffered drought year after year; Xun opened the granaries to relieve the poor, urged and supervised farming and sericulture, and the people depended on him.
translations.idiomatic: After years of drought he opened the granaries for the needy, pushed farming and silk production, and the county came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 時吳、會稽、丹楊多有伏匿，遜陳便宜，乞與幕焉。

translations.literal: At that time Wu, Kuaiji, and Danyang had many who hid in the hills; Xun submitted a memorial on what would be expedient, asking to be assigned to deal with them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits lurked widely in Wu, Kuaiji, and Danyang; Xun petitioned with a practical plan and asked to take the matter under his command.

sentences.zh: 會稽山賊大帥潘臨，舊為所在毒害，歷年不禽。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain of the Kuaiji hills, Pan Lin, had long ravaged the region and for years could not be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Lin, leader of the mountain bandits in Kuaiji, had plagued the countryside for years without being taken.

sentences.zh: 遜以手下召兵，討治深險，所向皆服，部曲已有二千餘人。

translations.literal: Xun raised troops from those under him, campaigned into the deepest fastnesses, and wherever he turned they submitted; his personal following already numbered over two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited soldiers locally, drove deep into the rugged terrain, and brought every pocket to heel until his command exceeded two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽賊帥尤突作亂，復往討之，拜定威校尉，軍屯利浦。

translations.literal: The bandit chief You Tu of Poyang rose in revolt; Xun went again to suppress him, was appointed Colonel Who Fixes Might, and encamped his army at Lipu.
translations.idiomatic: When You Tu of Poyang rebelled, Xun marched once more, earned appointment as Colonel Who Fixes Might, and quartered his troops at Lipu.

sentences.zh: 權以兄策女配遜，數訪世務。

translations.literal: Quan gave Xun his elder brother Ce's daughter in marriage and repeatedly consulted him on affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan married him to his elder brother Ce's daughter and often sought his counsel on statecraft.

sentences.zh: 遜建議曰：「方今英雄棋跱，豺狼規望，克敵寧亂。

translations.literal: Xun submitted advice: "At present heroes stand arrayed like pieces on a chessboard; wolves and jackals watch for openings—to defeat the enemy and pacify chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Xun urged: "The realm is locked in stalemate among rival warlords; jackals watch for any opening—only by crushing the foe can there be lasting calm."

sentences.zh: 非眾不濟，而山寇舊惡，依阻深地。

translations.literal: Without mass you cannot succeed, yet the mountain bandits are hardened evils ensconced in remote terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Numbers alone will not suffice while seasoned hill bandits hold the deep fastnesses.

sentences.zh: 夫腹心未平，難以圖遠，可大部伍，取其精銳。

translations.literal: If the heartland is not pacified, it is hard to plan far ahead; you should greatly enlarge the formations and draw out their crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: While rebellion festers at our core we cannot reach for distant goals—expand the armies and skim off their best fighters.

sentences.zh: 」權納其策，以為帳下右部督。

translations.literal: " Quan adopted his plan and appointed him commander of the right division under headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan accepted the proposal and named him commander of the headquarters right wing.

sentences.zh: 會丹楊賊帥費棧受曹公印綬，扇動山越，為作內應，權遣遜討棧。

translations.literal: It happened that the bandit chief Fei Zhan of Danyang had received seals and ribbons from Lord Cao, stirred up the mountain Yue to revolt, and arranged internal collusion; Quan sent Xun to campaign against Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: When Fei Zhan of Danyang took credentials from Cao Cao, incited the mountain tribes, and promised inside help, Sun Quan dispatched Xun against him.

sentences.zh: 棧支黨多而往兵少，遜乃益施牙幢，分佈鼓角，夜潛山谷間，鼓噪而前，應時破散。

translations.literal: Zhan's partisans were many but the troops sent were few; Xun therefore added more command banners, spread out drums and horns, slipped by night among the valleys, advanced with shouting and clamor, and at once broke and scattered them.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, Xun multiplied signal banners and drums, crept through the passes at night, and rolled forward with a sudden uproar that shattered Zhan's host.

sentences.zh: 遂部伍東三郡，強者為兵，羸者補戶，得精卒數萬人，宿惡蕩除，所過肅清，還屯蕪湖。

translations.literal: He then organized the people of the three eastern commanderies: the strong he made soldiers, the weak he registered as households, obtaining several tens of thousands of picked troops; long-standing evil was swept away, everywhere he passed was cleared, and he returned to encamp at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the three eastern commanderies—fit men into the ranks, the rest onto the tax rolls—and raised tens of thousands of veterans. Old bandit nests were cleared along his line of march before he pulled back to Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 會稽太守淳於式表遜枉取民人，愁擾所在。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Kuaiji, Chunyu Shi, memorialized that Xun had wrongfully seized common people and caused distress wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Shi of Kuaiji reported that Xun had pressed the populace unjustly and left a trail of misery.

sentences.zh: 遜後詣都，言次，稱式佳吏。

translations.literal: Later, when Xun came to the capital, in the course of conversation he praised Shi as a fine official.
translations.idiomatic: On a later visit to court he spoke well of Shi as an able administrator.

sentences.zh: 權曰：「式白君而君薦之，何也？

translations.literal: Quan said: "Shi denounced you, yet you recommend him—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked: "He impeached you—why sing his praises?"

sentences.zh: 」遜對曰：「式意欲養民，是以白遜。

translations.literal: " Xun replied: "Shi's intent was to nurture the people; therefore he reported me.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun answered: "His memorial aimed at protecting the common folk—that is why he singled me out.

sentences.zh: 若遜復毀式以亂聖聽，不可長也。

translations.literal: If I in turn slander Shi to confuse the sacred hearing, that cannot be encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Were I to strike back and blacken his name before Your Majesty, that habit must not be allowed to spread."

sentences.zh: 」權曰：「此誠長者之事，顧人不能為耳。

translations.literal: " Quan said: "This is truly the conduct of a man of maturity—only ordinary men cannot do it.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan said: "That is how an elder statesman behaves—few others could manage it."

sentences.zh: 」呂蒙稱疾詣建業，遜往見之。

translations.literal: " Lü Meng pleaded illness and went to Jianye; Xun went to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng claimed illness and traveled to Jianye; Xun called on him there.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「關羽接境，如何遠下，後不當可憂也？

translations.literal: He said to him: "Guan Yu borders us—how can you go far downstream? Will there not be cause for worry afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: Xun asked: "Guan Yu sits on our frontier—why leave for the lower Yangzi? Are we not inviting trouble behind our backs?"

sentences.zh: 」蒙曰：「誠如來言，然我病篤。

translations.literal: " Meng said: "It is indeed as you say, yet my illness is grave.
translations.idiomatic: " Lü Meng replied: "You are right—but I am desperately ill."

sentences.zh: 」遜曰：「羽矜其驍氣，陵轢於人。

translations.literal: " Xun said: "Yu prides himself on his fierce spirit and rides roughshod over others.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun said: "Guan Yu trusts his martial swagger and tramples everyone in his path.

sentences.zh: 始有大功，意驕志逸，但務北進，未嫌於我，有相聞病，必益無備。

translations.literal: Having lately won great merit, his mind is arrogant and his aims lax; he attends only to advancing north and bears us no suspicion; if word reaches him of illness, he will certainly grow even less prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from a triumph, he is swollen with pride and bent solely on the northern offensive; he hardly notices us. News of your sickness will only deepen his complacency.

sentences.zh: 今出其不意，自可禽制。

translations.literal: Now, catching him off guard, you can naturally seize and control him.
translations.idiomatic: Strike where he does not expect it and you can take him whole.

sentences.zh: 下見至尊，宜好為計。

translations.literal: When you go down to see the Supreme One, you ought to lay good plans.
translations.idiomatic: When you audience with the sovereign, work out the scheme in detail."

sentences.zh: 」蒙曰：「羽素勇猛，既難為敵，且已據荊州，恩信大行，兼始有功，膽勢益盛，未易圖也。

translations.literal: " Meng said: "Yu has always been fierce and brave; he is already hard to oppose as an enemy, and moreover he holds Jingzhou, where grace and trust run wide; coupled with his fresh merit, his daring and momentum grow stronger—not easy to scheme against.
translations.idiomatic: " Lü Meng said: "Guan Yu is redoubtable, holds Jingzhou with wide popularity, and rides a wave of recent victory—his boldness is peaking; he will not be easy to bring down."

sentences.zh: 」蒙至都，權問：「誰可代卿者？

translations.literal: " When Meng reached the capital, Quan asked: "Who can replace you?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Meng arrived at court, Sun Quan asked who could succeed him.

sentences.zh: 」蒙對曰：「陸遜意思深長，才堪負重，觀其規慮，終可大任。

translations.literal: " Meng replied: "Lu Xun's thought runs deep and far; his talent can bear heavy burdens; observe his plans and foresight—in the end he can take great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "Lu Xun thinks several moves ahead, shoulders weight well, and plans with steady judgment—he can eventually carry the highest charge.

sentences.zh: 而未有遠名，非羽所忌，無復是過。

translations.literal: Yet he has no distant reputation; Yu does not fear him—none surpasses him in this respect.
translations.idiomatic: He lacks fame abroad, so Guan Yu will not guard against him—no better choice exists.

sentences.zh: 若用之，當令外自韜隱，內察形便，然後可克。

translations.literal: If you employ him, you should make him outwardly conceal himself and inwardly observe terrain and advantage—then he can prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Use him, but let him play humble while studying the ground—only then can we win."

sentences.zh: 」權乃召遜，拜偏將軍右部督代蒙。

translations.literal: " Quan then summoned Xun and appointed him Lieutenant-General and commander of the right division to replace Meng.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan summoned Xun, commissioned him Lieutenant-General and right-wing commander, and sent him to succeed Lü Meng.

sentences.zh: 遜至陸口，書與羽曰：「前承觀釁而動，以律行師，小舉大克，一何巍巍!敵國敗績，利在同盟，聞慶拊節，想遂席捲，共獎王綱。

translations.literal: When Xun reached Lukou he wrote to Yu: "Earlier you watched for an opening and moved, conducted the army by regulation—a small effort, a great victory; how august! The foe state suffered rout; the gain lies with the alliance; hearing the news I clapped the beat of the verse and thought you would roll up the realm like a mat and together uphold the royal net.
translations.idiomatic: From Lukou Xun wrote to Guan Yu: "You seized the moment and struck by the book of war—small move, sweeping triumph. Our foe is broken; the ally profits. I rejoiced at the news and imagined you would overrun the field and help restore the imperial order."

sentences.zh: 近以不敏，受任來西，延慕光塵，思廩良規。

translations.literal: Lately, though unworthy, I have received assignment and come west; I long to walk in your wake and hope for your distinguished counsel.
translations.idiomatic: I am newly posted westward, unworthy as I am, and crave the honor of your dust—I hope for your seasoned guidance."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：

translations.literal: " He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He went on:

sentences.zh: 于禁等見獲，遐邇欣歎，以為將軍之勳足以長世，雖昔晉文城濮之師，淮陰拔趙之略，蔑以尚茲。

translations.literal: Yu Jin and others were captured; near and far rejoiced and sighed in admiration, holding that the General's merit suffices to endure for ages—even Duke Wen of Jin's army at Chengpu, the Huaiyin Lord's strategy against Zhao, does not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin fell into your hands, everyone marvelled: they said your fame would outlast the age—that even Duke Wen's victory at Chengpu or Han Xin's stroke against Zhao could not top it.

sentences.zh: 聞徐晃等少騎駐旌，窺望麾葆。

translations.literal: I hear that Xu Huang and others with a small body of cavalry have halted their banners and spy toward your standards and canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Word is that Xu Huang's light horse have halted within sight of your command banners and study your every move.

sentences.zh: 操猾虜也，忿不思難，恐潛增眾，以逞其心。

translations.literal: Cao is a cunning barbarian; in wrath he does not consider difficulties—I fear he may secretly swell his numbers to indulge his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao is wily; rage blinds him to risk, and he may be secretly reinforcing to get his way.

sentences.zh: 雖雲師老，猶有驍悍。

translations.literal: Although it is said the army is weary, it still has fierceness and toughness.
translations.idiomatic: They call his troops worn, yet they remain fierce.

sentences.zh: 且戰捷之後，常苦輕敵，古人杖術，軍勝彌警，願將軍廣為方計，以全獨克。

translations.literal: Moreover after battle triumph one commonly suffers from despising the enemy; the ancients relied on method—the more the army wins, the more vigilant; I wish the General would broadly devise stratagems to preserve sole victory.
translations.idiomatic: Victory breeds carelessness; the classics teach that the winning army must grow more alert. May you lay wider plans and clinch the triumph intact.

sentences.zh: 僕書生疏遲，忝所不堪。

translations.literal: I am dull and backward in letters and calligraphy—unworthy beyond endurance.
translations.idiomatic: I write clumsily and feel unworthy even of this note.

sentences.zh: 喜鄰威德，樂自傾盡。

translations.literal: I rejoice to neighbor your awesome virtue and am glad to pour myself out utterly.
translations.idiomatic: I delight in standing beside your prestige and would lay myself open to you entirely.

sentences.zh: 雖未合策，猶可懷也。

translations.literal: Although we have not yet joined in strategy, still there is room for cherishing.
translations.idiomatic: We have not yet coordinated plans, yet good will may still grow.

sentences.zh: 倘明注仰，有以察之。

translations.literal: If you will clearly fix your regard upward, there will be means by which to perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: If your noble eye should fall on me, you will see my sincerity."

sentences.zh: 羽覽遜書，有謙下自托之意，意大安，無復所嫌。

translations.literal: When Yu read Xun's letter, it had the intention of humility and self-abasement; his mind grew greatly at ease and he had no further suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Xun's flattering tone, Guan Yu relaxed completely and dropped his guard.

sentences.zh: 遜具啟形狀，陳其可禽之要。

translations.literal: Xun fully reported the situation and set forth the essentials by which Yu could be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Xun filed a detailed briefing that spelled out exactly how to seize Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 權乃潛軍而上，使遜與呂蒙為前部，至即克公安、南郡。

translations.literal: Quan then secretly advanced the army upstream, making Xun and Lü Meng the vanguard; on arrival they at once took Gong'an and Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan moved troops upstream in secret with Xun and Lü Meng leading the van; they stormed Gong'an and Nan Commandery as soon as they arrived.

sentences.zh: 遜徑進，領宜都太守，拜撫邊將軍，封華亭侯。

translations.literal: Xun pressed straight forward, took concurrent office as Administrator of Yidu, was appointed General Who Pacifies the Frontier, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Huating.
translations.idiomatic: Xun drove on, added Yidu to his portfolio, was named General Who Pacifies the Frontier, and received the marquisate of Huating.

sentences.zh: 備宜都太守樊友委郡走，諸城長吏及蠻夷君長皆降。

translations.literal: Bei's Administrator of Yidu, Fan You, abandoned the commandery and fled; the chief officials of the various cities and the chieftains of the Man and Yi all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei's prefect Fan You bolted from Yidu; every county seat and tribal head submitted.

sentences.zh: 遜請金銀銅印，以假授初附。

translations.literal: Xun requested gold, silver, and bronze seals to confer by temporary authority on those newly attached.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for gold, silver, and bronze seals to invest the newly surrendered officials.

sentences.zh: 是歲建安二十四年十一月也。

translations.literal: This was the eleventh month of the twenty-fourth year of the Jian'an era.
translations.idiomatic: It was the eleventh month of Jian'an 24 (219 CE).

sentences.zh: 遜遣將軍李異、謝旌等將三千人，攻蜀將詹晏、陳鳳。

translations.literal: Xun sent Generals Li Yi, Xie Jing, and others leading three thousand men to attack Shu generals Zhan Yan and Chen Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He detached Li Yi and Xie Jing with three thousand troops against Shu commanders Zhan Yan and Chen Feng.

sentences.zh: 異將水軍，旌將步兵，斷色險要，即破晏等，生降得鳳。

translations.literal: Yi commanded the navy, Jing commanded infantry; they seized the defiles and vital terrain, at once defeated Yan and the others, and captured Feng alive to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yi led the fleet, Jing the foot soldiers; they sealed the defiles, routed Yan's force, and took Feng prisoner.

sentences.zh: 又攻房陵太守鄧輔、南鄉太守郭睦，大破之。

translations.literal: They also attacked the Administrator of Fangling, Deng Fu, and the Administrator of Nanxiang, Guo Mu, and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: They went on to crush Deng Fu of Fangling and Guo Mu of Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 秭歸大姓文布、鄧凱等合夷兵數千人，首尾西方。

translations.literal: The great clansmen of Zigui, Wen Bu and Deng Kai and others, combined several thousand tribesmen and linked front and rear toward the west.
translations.idiomatic: The Zigui magnates Wen Bu and Deng Kai rallied thousands of tribal warriors and coordinated operations toward the western front.

sentences.zh: 遜復部旌討破布、凱。

translations.literal: Xun again deployed Jing to campaign against and defeat Bo and Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent Jing back out and broke Wen Bu and Deng Kai.

sentences.zh: 布凱脫走，蜀以為將。

translations.literal: Bo and Kai broke away and fled; Shu appointed them generals.
translations.idiomatic: Bo and Kai escaped and Liu Bei commissioned them as generals.

sentences.zh: 遜令人誘之，布帥眾還降。

translations.literal: Xun ordered men to lure them; Bo led the multitude back to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xun baited them with promises until Wen Bo brought his followers over intact.

sentences.zh: 前後斬獲招納，凡數萬計。

translations.literal: Before and after, those beheaded, captured, and induced to submit amounted to several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Kills, prisoners, and defectors ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 權以遜為右護軍、鎮西將軍，進封婁侯。

translations.literal: Quan appointed Xun Right Protector of the Army and General Who Guards the West, advancing his enfeoffment to Marquis of Lou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named him Right Protector of the Army and General Who Guards the West and promoted his fief to Marquis of Lou.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：权嘉逊功德，欲殊显之，虽为上将军列侯，犹欲令历本州举命，乃使扬州牧吕范就辟别驾从事，举茂才。〉

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: Quan admired Xun's merit and virtue and wished to display him exceptionally; although he was already senior general and a ranked marquis, he still wished him to undergo nomination in his native province, and therefore ordered the Governor of Yangzhou, Lü Fan, to summon him as aide-de-camp and recommend him as flourishing talent.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu notes that Sun Quan prized Xun's record and wanted him honored beyond his rank as senior general and marquis—he even had Yangzhou Governor Lü Fan formally summon him as aide and nominate him "flourishing talent" for his home province.

sentences.zh: 時荊州士人新還，仕進或未得所，遜上疏曰：「昔漢高受命，招延英異，光武中興，群俊畢至，苟可以熙隆道教者，未必遠近。

translations.literal: At that time Jingzhou scholars had newly returned, and their advancement in office had perhaps not found its proper place; Xun submitted a memorial: "In old days when Han Gaozu received the mandate, he summoned the extraordinary and unusual; when Guangwu restored the dynasty, all the talented arrived—if they could brighten and exalt the teaching of the Way, they need not be judged by nearness or distance.
translations.idiomatic: Many Jingzhou literati had just come over and still lacked suitable posts. Xun memorialized: "Gaozu drew talent from every quarter; Guangwu's revival brought every able man forward—whoever could strengthen the moral order mattered, whether from far or near.

sentences.zh: 今荊州始定，人物未達，臣愚慺慺，乞普加覆載抽拔之恩。

translations.literal: Now Jingzhou is newly stabilized and men of ability have not yet risen—I, foolish and earnest, beg that universally there be added the grace of covering and bearing up and drawing forth and elevating.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou is only just pacified and men of talent remain obscure; I humbly ask that you extend shelter and promotion across the board.

sentences.zh: 令並獲自進，然後四海延頸，思歸大化。

translations.literal: Order that together they may obtain self-advancement—then within the four seas all will crane their necks and think to return to great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Let each find his path to office, and the whole realm will turn willingly toward your civilizing rule."

sentences.zh: 」權敬納其言。

translations.literal: " Quan respectfully adopted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan accepted the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 夷陵要害，國之關限，雖為易得，亦復易失。

translations.literal: Yiling is a critical point, the border bar of the state; though it is easy to obtain, it is likewise easy to lose.
translations.idiomatic: Yiling is a choke point of the realm—quick to take, quick to lose.

sentences.zh: 失之非徒損一郡之地，荊州可憂。

translations.literal: To lose it is not merely to damage the territory of one commandery—Jingzhou is to be worried over.
translations.idiomatic: Losing it means more than one commandery; all of Jingzhou would be in peril.

sentences.zh: 今日爭之，當令必諧。

translations.literal: Today in contesting it, we ought to make certain it succeeds.
translations.idiomatic: This fight must end in success.

sentences.zh: 備干天常，不守窟穴，而敢自送。

translations.literal: Bei offends heaven's constant order; he does not guard his burrow but dares to deliver himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei defies natural order: instead of holding his lair he walks into our trap.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不材，憑奉威靈，以順討逆，破壞在近。

translations.literal: I, though lacking talent, relying on and receiving awesome spiritual power, with the compliant attack the rebellious—destruction and ruin are near.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy as I am, I ride your majesty's mandate to punish the rebel—his collapse is at hand.

sentences.zh: 尋備前後行軍，多敗少成。

translations.literal: Tracing Bei's former and later campaigns with armies, many defeats, few successes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei's past campaigns show mostly defeat, seldom victory.

sentences.zh: 推此論之，不足為戚。

translations.literal: Pushing this argument to its conclusion, he is not sufficient to be an object of anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: By that measure he is hardly worth fretting over.

sentences.zh: 臣初嫌之，水陸俱進，今反捨船就步，處處結營，察其佈置，必無他變。

translations.literal: I at first was troubled that he would advance by water and land together; now on the contrary he abandons boats and takes to foot, everywhere tying camps—observing his disposition, there will certainly be no other change.
translations.idiomatic: I feared a combined river and land thrust; now he has left his boats for dry ground and strung camps everywhere—his options are spent.

sentences.zh: 伏願至尊高枕，不以為念也。

translations.literal: I humbly wish the Supreme One to pillow high and not take it to mind.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty rest easy—there is no cause for concern."

sentences.zh: 諸將並曰：「攻備當在初，今乃令人五六百里，相銜持經七八月，其諸要害皆以固守，擊之必無利矣。

translations.literal: The generals together said: "Attacking Bei ought to have been at the beginning; now it has made men extend five or six hundred li, mutually locked in stalemate through seven or eight months; all the critical points are already firmly guarded—to strike them certainly holds no advantage.
translations.idiomatic: The officers objected: "We should have hit Liu Bei at once. Now we have chased him five or six hundred li and sparred for most of a year; every defile is dug in—an assault gains nothing."

sentences.zh: 」遜曰：「備是猾虜，更嘗事多，其軍始集，思慮精專，未可干也。

translations.literal: " Xun said: "Bei is a cunning barbarian; he has experienced much in affairs; his army is newly gathered, his thought and planning concentrated and focused—not to be opposed.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun replied: "Liu Bei is wily and battle-tested. His host just assembled—focus and discipline are at their peak; do not engage yet.

sentences.zh: 今住己久，不得我便，兵疲意沮，計不復生，掎角此寇，正在今日。

translations.literal: Now they have stayed long and obtained no advantage from us; the troops are weary and the will disheartened; stratagems are no longer born—pincering this bandit is precisely today.
translations.idiomatic: They have stalled without gaining leverage; men are tired and schemes exhausted—the moment to crush them is now.

sentences.zh: 」乃先攻一營，不利。

translations.literal: " He therefore first attacked one camp; it went badly.
translations.idiomatic: He tried one camp first and was thrown back.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「空殺兵耳。

translations.literal: All the generals said: "It is merely empty killing of soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The generals grumbled: "We are only wasting men."

sentences.zh: 」遜曰：「吾已曉破之之術。

translations.literal: " Xun said: "I already understand the method of breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun said: "I know how to break them now."

sentences.zh: 」乃敕各持一把茅，以火攻拔之。

translations.literal: " He therefore ordered each to hold a bundle of thatch and by fire attack seize them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every man to carry straw and take the camps by fire.

sentences.zh: 一爾勢成，通率諸軍同時俱攻，斬張南、馮習及胡王沙靡柯等首，破其四十餘營。

translations.literal: As soon as thus the momentum formed, he led through all the armies simultaneously together attacking, beheaded Zhang Nan, Feng Xi, and the Hu king Shamoke and others, and broke more than forty of their camps.
translations.idiomatic: Once the blaze caught, he threw every column forward at once, slew Zhang Nan, Feng Xi, and the tribal king Shamoke, and overran more than forty camps.

sentences.zh: 備將杜路、劉寧等窮逼請降。

translations.literal: Bei's generals Du Lu, Liu Ning, and others, pressed to extremity, requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Du Lu, Liu Ning, and other Shu officers surrendered when trapped.

sentences.zh: 備升馬鞍山，陳兵自繞。

translations.literal: Bei ascended Horse Saddle Mountain and arrayed troops encircling himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei gained Ma'an Mountain and drew his lines in a ring.

sentences.zh: 遜督促諸軍四面蹙之，土崩瓦解，死者萬數。

translations.literal: Xun urged and supervised all the armies to press him from four sides; earth collapsed and tiles shattered; the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Xun closed every side; the Shu army collapsed with tens of thousands dead.

sentences.zh: 備因夜遁，驛人自擔燒鐃鎧斷後，僅得入白帝城。

translations.literal: Bei therefore fled by night; relay men themselves carrying burned cymbals and armor covered the rear; he barely was able to enter Baidi City.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei fled by night; couriers hauled away armor and gear to cover his retreat, and he barely reached Baidi.

sentences.zh: 其舟船器械，水步軍資，一時略盡，屍骸漂流，塞江而下。

translations.literal: Their boats, ships, weapons, and gear, water and foot army supplies, in one moment were almost entirely gone; corpses drifted and floated, jamming the river downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Ships, weapons, and supplies vanished in a stroke; bodies choked the river.

sentences.zh: 備大慚恚，曰：「吾乃為遜所折辱，豈非天邪!」

translations.literal: Bei was greatly ashamed and resentful, saying: "I have been humiliated by Xun—is it not heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei groaned in shame: "To be broken by Lu Xun—can this be anything but fate?"

sentences.zh: 初，孫桓別討備前鋒於夷道，為備所圍，求救於遜。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Sun Huan separately campaigned against Bei's vanguard at Yidao, was surrounded by Bei, and requested rescue from Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sun Huan had struck Liu Bei's van at Yidao, been surrounded, and begged Xun for relief.

sentences.zh: 遜曰：「未可。

translations.literal: Xun said: "Not yet.
translations.idiomatic: Xun answered: "Not yet."

sentences.zh: 」諸將曰：「孫安東公族，見圍已困，奈何不救？

translations.literal: The generals said: "Lord Sun the East of the River is of the ducal house; he is seen besieged and already in straits—how can we not rescue him?"
translations.idiomatic: The officers protested: "Sun Huan is a son of the house, ringed and in trouble—how can we leave him?"

sentences.zh: 」遜曰：「安東得士眾心，城牢糧足，無可憂也。

translations.literal: Xun said: "The East of the River has won the hearts of officers and men; the walls are strong and the grain ample—there is nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Xun replied: "Huan holds the garrison's loyalty; the walls and granaries are sound—he is in no real danger.

sentences.zh: 待吾計展，欲不救安東，安東自解。

translations.literal: Wait until my plan unfolds; even if we do not rescue the East of the River, the East of the River will free himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once my design runs its course, he will break the siege without a relief column."

sentences.zh: 」及方略大施，備果奔潰。

translations.literal: " When the grand strategy was fully deployed, Bei indeed broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the plan matured, Liu Bei routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 桓後見遜曰：「前實怨不見救，定至今日，乃知調度自有方耳。

translations.literal: Later Huan saw Xun and said: "Earlier I truly resented not seeing rescue; fixed until today, only now do I know that direction and deployment had their own method.
translations.idiomatic: Huan later told Xun: "I cursed you for not coming—only now do I see your dispositions were sound."

sentences.zh: 」當御備時，諸將軍或是孫策時舊將，或公室貴戚，各自矜恃，不相聽從。

translations.literal: " When opposing Bei, the various generals were either old commanders from Sun Ce's time or noble kin of the ducal house; each relied on his own pride and did not obey one another.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liu Bei campaign the generals—veterans of Sun Ce or royal in-laws—each trusted his own judgment and ignored orders.

sentences.zh: 遜案劍曰：

translations.literal: Xun grasped his sword and said:
translations.idiomatic: Xun gripped his sword hilt and declared:

sentences.zh: 劉備天下知名，曹操所憚，今在境界，此強對也。

translations.literal: Liu Bei is famous under heaven; he is one whom Cao Cao esteems as dangerous; now he is within our borders—this is a formidable opponent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei is known throughout the realm—even Cao Cao counted him a serious rival. He stands on our borders now: a dangerous enemy.

sentences.zh: 諸君並荷國恩，當相輯睦，共剪此虜，上報所受，而不相順，非所謂也。

translations.literal: You gentlemen alike bear the state's grace; you ought to harmonize with one another, together shear off this captive, and upward repay what you have received—yet you do not defer to one another; this is not what is called for.
translations.idiomatic: You all owe the dynasty your careers; you should stand together, destroy this enemy, and repay the throne—not pull in separate directions.

sentences.zh: 僕雖書生，受命主上。

translations.literal: I, though a mere scholar, have received mandate from the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: I am only a scholar, yet the sovereign has placed command in my hands.

sentences.zh: 國家所以屈諸君使相承望者，以僕有尺寸可稱，能忍辱負重故也。

translations.literal: The reason the state bends you gentlemen to make you defer to one another is that I have some small merit that may be praised and am able to endure shame and bear heavy burden.
translations.idiomatic: The court asks you to defer to me because I have earned a little trust and can swallow pride for the common good.

sentences.zh: 各在其事，豈復得辭！

translations.literal: Each is in his task—how can there again be excuse!
translations.idiomatic: Each of you has his duty—there is no room for refusal!

sentences.zh: 軍令有常，不可犯矣。

translations.literal: Military orders have constancy; they may not be violated.
translations.idiomatic: These orders stand—defy them at your peril."

sentences.zh: 及至破備，計多出遜，諸將乃服。

translations.literal: When it came to defeating Bei, the plans mostly came from Xun; only then did the generals submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei fell, most of the winning moves had been Xun's; the generals finally conceded.

sentences.zh: 權聞之，曰：「君何以初不啟諸將違節度者邪？

translations.literal: When Quan heard of it, he said: "Why did you at first not report the generals who violated command?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked: "Why did you not report the commanders who disobeyed earlier?"

sentences.zh: 」遜對曰：「受恩深重，任過其才。

translations.literal: Xun replied: "I received grace deep and heavy; the duty exceeded my talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xun said: "Your favor toward me runs deep, yet the burden outstripped my ability.

sentences.zh: 又此諸將或任腹心，或堪爪牙，或是功臣，皆國家所當與共克定大事者。

translations.literal: Moreover these generals are either employed as heart and belly, or suitable as fangs and claws, or are merit subjects—all are ones the state ought to join with to overcome and settle great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Those men are your inner circle, your sword arm, your battle-tested veterans—the state needs every one of them for the great work ahead."

sentences.zh: 臣雖駑懦，竊慕相如、寇恂相下之義，以濟國事。

translations.literal: I, though dull and weak, privately admire the meaning by which Xiangru and Kou Xun yielded to one another, so as to aid state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I am slow and timid, yet I hoped to emulate Lin Xiangru and Kou Xun—yielding for the sake of the realm."

sentences.zh: 」權大笑稱善，加拜遜輔國將軍，領荊州牧，即改封江陵候。

translations.literal: " Quan laughed greatly and praised it as good, additionally appointing Xun General Who Supports the State, concurrent Governor of Jingzhou, and at once changing his enfeoffment to Marquis of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan laughed and approved. He promoted Xun to General Who Supports the State with concurrent tenure as Governor of Jingzhou and transferred his fief to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 又備既住白帝，徐盛、潘璋、宋謙等各競表言備必可禽，乞復攻之。

translations.literal: Moreover, after Bei had lodged at Baidi, Xu Sheng, Pan Zhang, Song Qian, and others each vied in memorials saying Bei could certainly be captured, begging to attack him again.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Bei held Baidi, Xu Sheng, Pan Zhang, Song Qian, and others competed in memorials insisting he could be taken and urging another strike.

sentences.zh: 權以問遜，遜與朱然、駱統以為「曹丕大合士眾。

translations.literal: Quan put the question to Xun; Xun together with Zhu Ran and Luo Tong held that "Cao Pi is greatly assembling soldiers and masses.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan consulted Xun, who with Zhu Ran and Luo Tong argued that Cao Pi was massing a large host.

sentences.zh: 外托助國討備，內實有奸心，謹決計輒還」。

translations.literal: Outwardly he pretends to aid the state in campaigning against Bei; inwardly he truly harbors treacherous intent—we respectfully resolve on the plan to return at once."
translations.idiomatic: He claims to help us against Liu Bei but schemes inside—we should withdraw immediately."

sentences.zh: 無幾，魏軍果出，三方受敵也。

translations.literal: Before long, Wei armies indeed came forth; on three sides they received enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wei struck, and Wu faced enemies on three fronts.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：刘备闻魏军大出，书与逊云：「贼今已在江陵，吾将复东，将军谓其能然不？

translations.literal: The Wu Records states: When Liu Bei heard that Wei armies had come forth in force, he wrote to Xun saying: "The bandits are now already at Jiangling; I will again go east—does the General think they can do it or not?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Records says Liu Bei, learning of Wei's offensive, wrote to Xun: "The enemy has reached Jiangling; I mean to march east again—do you think they can pull it off?"

sentences.zh: 」逊答曰：「但恐军新破，创痍未复，始求通亲，且当自补，未暇穷兵耳。

translations.literal: Xun answered: "I only fear the army is newly broken, wounds not yet healed; they have begun seeking kinship by marriage and ought for the moment to repair themselves—they have no leisure to exhaust military force.
translations.idiomatic: Xun replied: "Their army is fresh from defeat and still licking wounds; they seek ties by marriage and must rebuild—they are in no shape for total war.

sentences.zh: 若不惟算，欲复以倾覆之餘，远送以来者，无所逃命。」〉

translations.literal: If they do not reckon carefully and wish again with the remnants of rout to send from afar those who come, there will be nowhere to escape life."
translations.idiomatic: If they misjudge and drive their beaten scraps east again, they will find nowhere to run."

sentences.zh: 備尋病亡，子禪襲位，諸葛亮秉政，與權連和。

translations.literal: Not long after Bei sickened and died; his son Shan succeeded the throne; Zhuge Liang held the government and allied with Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei soon died. His son Shan succeeded, Zhuge Liang took the reins, and Shu renewed its pact with Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 時事所宜，權輒令遜語亮，並刻權印，以置遜所。

translations.literal: As affairs of the time required, Quan always ordered Xun to speak to Liang, and moreover carved Quan's seal and placed it at Xun's residence.
translations.idiomatic: When policy required, Sun Quan had Xun negotiate with Zhuge Liang and even left an impressed seal at Xun's command.

sentences.zh: 權每與禪、亮書，常過示遜，輕重可否，有所不安，便令改定，以印封行之。

translations.literal: Whenever Quan wrote letters to Shan and Liang, he always passed them to show Xun; on weighty matters of yes or no, if something was unsettling, he then ordered them revised and fixed, and with seal impressed enacted them.
translations.idiomatic: Letters to Liu Shan and Zhuge Liang crossed Xun's desk first; if wording troubled him, Sun Quan had it revised, sealed, and sent.

sentences.zh: 七年，權使鄱陽太守周魴譎魏大司馬曹休。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Quan ordered the Administrator of Poyang, Zhou Fang, to deceive Wei's Grand Marshal Cao Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Huangwu (228 CE), Sun Quan had Poyang prefect Zhou Fang lure Wei's Grand Marshal Cao Xiu into a trap.

sentences.zh: 休果舉眾入皖，乃召遜假黃鉞，為大都督，逆休。

translations.literal: Xiu indeed raised the host and entered Wan; Quan then summoned Xun, lent him the yellow battle-axe, made him commander-in-chief, and opposed Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu marched into Wan as hoped; Sun Quan invested Xun with the yellow axe as commander-in-chief to meet him.

sentences.zh: 〈陆机为逊铭曰：魏大司马曹休侵我北鄙，乃假公黄钺，统御六师及中军禁卫而摄行王事，主上执鞭，百司屈膝。

translations.literal: Lu Ji's inscription for Xun states: When Wei Grand Marshal Cao Xiu invaded our northern border, they lent the Duke the yellow battle-axe; he commanded the six armies and the palace guards and acted in the king's affairs; the sovereign held the whip; all offices bent the knee.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's epitaph says that when Cao Xiu struck the northern frontier, Xun received the yellow axe, commanded the field armies and imperial guards in the ruler's name, while Sun Quan stood by with whip in hand and every minister bowed.

sentences.zh: 吴录曰：假逊黄钺，吴王亲执鞭以见之。〉

translations.literal: The Wu Records states: Xun was lent the yellow battle-axe; the King of Wu personally held the whip to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Records adds that the King of Wu saw him off holding the carriage whip."

sentences.zh: 休既覺知，恥見欺誘，自恃兵馬精多，遂交戰。

translations.literal: When Xiu became aware, he was ashamed at being deceived and lured; relying on his troops and horses being refined and numerous, he then joined battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Xiu realized the ruse, shame and pride drove him to fight—he trusted his superior numbers.

sentences.zh: 遜自為中部，令朱桓、全琮為左右冀，三道俱近，果沖休伏兵，因驅走之，追亡逐北，逕至夾石，斬獲萬餘，牛馬騾驢車乘萬輛，軍資器械略盡。

translations.literal: Xun himself was the center division; he ordered Zhu Huan and Quan Zong to be left and right wings; on three roads they all drew near; they indeed burst Xiu's ambush troops and thereby drove them in flight, pursued the fleeing and chased the north, straight to Jiashi; beheadings and captures exceeded ten thousand; oxen, horses, mules, donkeys, and vehicles numbered ten thousand loads; military supplies and weapons were almost entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: Xun held the center with Zhu Huan and Quan Zong on the wings. Their converging columns smashed Cao Xiu's ambush and routed him to Jiashi. They killed or captured over ten thousand men, seized ten thousand head of livestock and carts, and stripped Wei's baggage train bare.

sentences.zh: 休還，疽發背死。

translations.literal: Xiu returned; a boil broke out on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu withdrew and died of a carbuncle on his back.

sentences.zh: 諸軍振旅過武昌，權令左右以御蓋覆遜，入出殿門。

translations.literal: The various armies shook the host and passed Wuchang; Quan ordered those at his sides to cover Xun with the imperial canopy, entering and exiting the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched past Wuchang in triumph; Sun Quan had attendants shade Xun with the imperial umbrella through the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 凡所賜遜，皆御物上珍，於時莫與為比。

translations.literal: All that was bestowed on Xun were imperial objects and supreme treasures; at the time none could be compared to him.
translations.idiomatic: The gifts were palace treasures without parallel.

sentences.zh: 遣還西陵。

translations.literal: He was sent back to Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent back to his post at Xiling.

sentences.zh: 臣以為科法嚴峻，下犯者多。

translations.literal: Your subject believes the statutes and laws are harsh and severe; those below who offend are many.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes are harsh, and those who run afoul of them are legion.

sentences.zh: 頃年以來，將吏罹罪，雖不慎可責，然天下未一，當圖近取，小宜恩貸，以安下情。

translations.literal: In recent years generals and clerks have suffered crimes; although incaution may be blamed, yet the realm under heaven is not yet one; one ought to plan near gains; on small matters grace and leniency should be applied, so as to pacify feeling below.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders and clerks keep falling foul of the law—some deserve blame, yet the empire is not united; we should pursue practical gains and grant minor offenses clemency to steady morale.

sentences.zh: 且世務日興，良能為先，自非奸穢人身，難忍之過，乞復顯用，展其力效。

translations.literal: Moreover worldly affairs daily rise; able capability comes first; unless it be wicked filth in the person or unbearable fault, I beg to restore them to evident employment and extend their strength and effect.
translations.idiomatic: Business multiplies daily and ability matters most. Unless a man is irredeemably corrupt, I ask that proven offenders be reinstated so their talents serve the state.

sentences.zh: 此乃聖王忘過記功，以成王業。

translations.literal: This is how a sage king forgets faults and records merit, thereby completing kingly enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: That is how sage kings overlook slips and remember service—how dynasties are built.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高捨陳平之愆，用其奇略，終建勳祚，功垂千載。

translations.literal: In old days Han Gaozu set aside Chen Ping's offenses and employed his strange stratagems; in the end he established merit and fortune; the achievement hangs for a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu forgave Chen Ping's lapses and used his stratagems—glory that still echoes after a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 夫峻法嚴刑，非帝王之隆業；

translations.literal: As for harsh laws and severe punishments, these are not the flourishing enterprise of an emperor-king;
translations.idiomatic: Draconian law is no foundation for lasting rule;

sentences.zh: 有罰無怒，非懷遠弘規也。

translations.literal: having punishments without wrath is not the grand norm for cherishing the distant.
translations.idiomatic: punishment without rage is no blueprint for winning distant peoples."

sentences.zh: 權欲遣偏師取夷州及朱崖，皆以咨遜，遜上疏曰：

translations.literal: Quan wished to dispatch a detached force to take Yizhou and Zhuya; on all these he consulted Xun; Xun submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan planned expeditions to Yizhou (Taiwan) and Hainan, he asked Xun, who replied in a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為四海未定，當須民力，以濟時務。

translations.literal: Your foolish subject believes the four seas are not yet settled; one must rely on the people's strength to aid the tasks of the times.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still divided; the state must husband popular strength for urgent tasks.

sentences.zh: 今兵興歷年，見眾損減，陛下憂勞聖慮。

translations.literal: Now armies have risen year after year; the visible host diminishes and declines; Your Majesty's sagely cares labor with anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Years of campaigning have thinned our ranks while Your Majesty wears yourself out with worry.

sentences.zh: 忘寢與食，將遠規夷州，以定大事，臣反覆思惟。

translations.literal: You forget sleep and food and intend far to plan Yizhou so as to settle great affairs; your subject turns it over repeatedly in thought.
translations.idiomatic: You skip meals and sleep to mount a distant strike on Yiz—I have weighed it again and again.

sentences.zh: 未見其利，萬里襲取，風波難測，民易水土，必致疾疫，今驅見眾，經涉不毛，欲益更損，欲利反害。

translations.literal: I do not see its benefit; to raid and seize ten thousand li away, wind and waves are hard to fathom; the people change water and soil and surely will bring plague and epidemic; now driving the visible host to traverse barren lands—seeking increase will further diminish; seeking profit will return harm.
translations.idiomatic: I see no gain: an assault across open ocean invites unpredictable seas and sickness when troops swap climates. Marching our depleted armies through barren islands promises loss, not profit.

sentences.zh: 又珠崖絕險，民猶禽獸，得其民不足濟事，無其兵不足虧眾。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhuya is utterly perilous; the people are still like birds and beasts—obtaining their people is not enough to aid affairs; lacking their troops is not enough to diminish our masses.
translations.idiomatic: Hainan is deadly terrain and its folk barely settled—its villages would not help us, and skipping them would not weaken us.

sentences.zh: 今江東見眾，自足圖事，但當畜力而後動耳。

translations.literal: Now the visible host east of the Yangzi is itself sufficient to plan affairs—only one ought to store strength and afterward move.
translations.idiomatic: Our Jiangdong armies suffice for our aims—we should husband strength and strike only when ready.

sentences.zh: 昔桓王創基，兵不一旅，而開大業。

translations.literal: In old days King Huan laid the foundation; his soldiers were not even one brigade, yet he opened great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huan began with fewer than a regiment yet carved out a realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下承運，拓定江表。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has received the mandate and expanded and settled the south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: You inherited the mandate and pacified the south.

sentences.zh: 臣聞治亂討逆，須兵為威，農桑衣食，民這本業，而干戈未戢，民有饑寒。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that ordering chaos and punishing rebellion require troops as awesomeness; farming and sericulture, clothing and food are the people's root occupation—yet weapons of war are not yet stored away; the people have hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion requires armies to overawe it, yet farming and silk are the people's foundation—war still rages and families go cold and hungry.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜育養士民，寬其祖賦，眾克在和，義以勸勇，則河渭可平，九有一統矣。

translations.literal: Your foolish subject believes it is fitting to nurture and rear scholars and commoners, widen their rent and taxes, the masses overcome when there is harmony; with righteousness encourage bravery—then He and Wei may be pacified and the nine provinces unified.
translations.idiomatic: Nurture the people, lighten taxes, keep harmony in the ranks, and rally courage with justice—the Central Plains will yield and the nine regions unite."

sentences.zh: 權遂征夷州，得不補失。

translations.literal: Quan then campaigned against Yizhou; what was gained did not repay what was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan invaded Yizhou anyway and gained less than it cost.

sentences.zh: 及公孫淵背盟，權欲往征。

translations.literal: When Gongsun Yuan betrayed the covenant, Quan wished to go campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongsun Yuan broke the alliance, Sun Quan meant to lead an expedition himself.

sentences.zh: 遜上疏曰：

translations.literal: Xun submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xun answered with a memorial:

sentences.zh: 淵憑險恃固，拘留大使，名馬不獻，實可仇忿。

translations.literal: Yuan relies on peril and trusts in solidity; he detains the grand envoy; famed horses he does not present—truly one may hate and resent.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yuan holds the rugged northeast, holds our envoy hostage, and withholds promised horses—cause enough for wrath.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷猾夏，未染王化，鳥竄荒裔，拒逆王師，至令陛下愛赫斯怒，欲勞萬乘泛輕越海，不慮其危而涉不測。

translations.literal: The Man and Yi vex the Huaxia; they have not been touched by royal transformation; like birds they dart to wild borderlands, resisting the royal army—so Your Majesty is moved to righteous wrath and would labor the host to float lightly across the sea, not reckoning the danger of crossing the unfathomable.
translations.idiomatic: Those tribes beyond civilization flit along the frontier and defy imperial troops—yet Your Majesty would brave the sea on account of insult, heedless of peril.

sentences.zh: 方今天下雲擾，群雄虎爭，英豪踴躍，張聲大視。

translations.literal: Just now under heaven clouds of turmoil stir; many heroes contend like tigers; heroic champions leap and bound; they spread reputation and gaze broadly.
translations.idiomatic: The realm boils with rivals who posture and strike like tigers.

sentences.zh: 陛下以神武之姿，涎膺期運，破操烏林，敗備西陵，禽羽荊州，斯三虜者當世雄傑。

translations.literal: Your Majesty with divine martial bearing received the timely mandate; you broke Cao at Wulin, defeated Bei at Xiling, captured Yu at Jingzhou—these three captives were heroes of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty in martial splendor answered heaven's call—you crushed Cao at Wulin, broke Liu Bei at Xiling, took Guan Yu in Jingzhou: those three were the age's champions.

sentences.zh: 皆摧其鋒。

translations.literal: All had their sharp points broken.
translations.idiomatic: You broke each at the height of his power.

sentences.zh: 聖化所綏，萬里草偃，方蕩平華夏，總一大猷。

translations.literal: Where sagely transformation pacifies, ten thousand li the grass bends low; you are just now sweeping flat the Huaxia and gathering the one great plan.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue bows the grass for a thousand leagues—you are on the verge of unifying the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 今不忍小忿，而發雷霆之怒，違垂堂之戒，輕萬乘之重，此臣之所惑也。

translations.literal: Now you cannot bear a small resentment yet unleash thunder's wrath; you violate the warning about the high hall; you slight the weight of the ten thousand carriages—this is what confuses your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Yet over a slight insult you would thunder forth, ignore the caution about leaning from high halls, and hazard the realm—that puzzles me.

sentences.zh: 臣聞志行萬里者，不中道而輟足；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that those who intend to walk ten thousand li do not halfway cease foot;
translations.idiomatic: They say the traveler bound for a distant goal does not quit halfway;

sentences.zh: 圖四海者，匪懷細以害大。

translations.literal: those who plot the four seas do not harbor the petty to harm the great.
translations.idiomatic: those who would rule the world do not sacrifice the whole for a trifle.

sentences.zh: 強寇在境，荒服未庭，陛下乘桴遠征，必致窺闟，戚至而憂，悔之無及。

translations.literal: Strong bandits are at the borders; the wild outer zones have not come to court; Your Majesty rides the raft on distant campaign—surely it will bring spying at the inner gates; when calamity arrives then worry, regret will not reach.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful enemies ring us while distant tribes withhold tribute. A raft-borne expedition invites rivals to probe our heartland—by the time disaster strikes, regret is useless.

sentences.zh: 若使大事時捷，則淵不討自服；

translations.literal: If you cause great affairs timely to succeed, then Yuan without campaigning will himself submit;
translations.idiomatic: Win the greater contest elsewhere and Gongsun Yuan will kneel without a blow;

sentences.zh: 今乃遠惜遼東眾之與馬，奈何獨欲捐江東萬安之本業而不借乎？

translations.literal: now you instead cherish from afar Liaodong's masses and horses—how can you alone wish to cast away Jiangdong's foundation of ten thousand securities and not borrow?
translations.idiomatic: why fuss over Liaodong's horses and foot soldiers while risking Jiangdong's secure foundation?

sentences.zh: 乞息六師，以威大虜，早定中夏，垂耀將來。

translations.literal: I beg to rest the six armies, thereby awe the great captive; early settle the central Xia; let glory hang for the future.
translations.idiomatic: Rest the armies, overawe the foe by reputation alone, secure the Central Plains first, and leave glory for posterity."

sentences.zh: 權用納焉。

translations.literal: Quan employed and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾五年，權北征。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiahe, Quan campaigned north.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiahe 5 (236 CE) Sun Quan marched north.

sentences.zh: 使遜與諸葛瑾攻襄陽。

translations.literal: He ordered Xun together with Zhuge Jin to attack Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xun with Zhuge Jin against Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 遜遣親人韓扁□表奉報，還。

translations.literal: Xun sent his kinsman Han Bian to deliver a memorial for submission and await response; Bian returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent his man Han Bian to court with a memorial and bring back the sovereign's answer.

sentences.zh: 遇敵於沔中，鈔邏得扁。

translations.literal: They encountered the enemy in the Mian region; raiding patrol captured Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei patrols on the Han River seized Han Bian.

sentences.zh: 瑾聞之甚懼。

translations.literal: When Jin heard of it he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jin was terrified.

sentences.zh: 書與遜云：「大駕已旋，賊得韓扁，具知吾闊狹。

translations.literal: He wrote to Xun saying: "The great chariot has already returned; the bandits obtained Han Bian and fully know our breadth and narrowness.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Xun: "The sovereign has withdrawn; the enemy captured Han Bian and knows our whole disposition.

sentences.zh: 且水干，宜當急去。

translations.literal: Moreover the water is dry; it is fitting that we urgently depart.
translations.idiomatic: The river is falling—we must pull out fast."

sentences.zh: 」遜未答，方催人種葑豆，與諸將欒棋射戲如常。

translations.literal: Xun did not reply; he was just urging men to plant turnips and beans; with the various generals he played weiqi and shooting games as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Xun did not answer. He ordered radish and bean planting and played weiqi and archery with his officers as if nothing were wrong.

sentences.zh: 瑾曰：「伯言多智略，其當有以。

translations.literal: Jin said: "Boyan has much wisdom and stratagem; he ought to have a reason.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jin said: "Boyan is too clever not to have a plan."

sentences.zh: 」自來見遜，遜曰：「賊知大駕以旋，無所復戚，得專力於吾。

translations.literal: He himself came to see Xun; Xun said: "The bandits know the great chariot has returned; they have nothing further to worry about; they obtain concentrated force against us.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Xun, who said: "Wei knows Your Majesty has withdrawn—they need no longer guard Luoyang and can focus everything on us.

sentences.zh: 又已守要害之處，兵將意動，且當自定以安之，施設變術，然後出耳。

translations.literal: Moreover they already guard critical places; soldiers and generals' intents stir—for the moment one ought to settle oneself to pacify them, deploy and arrange shifting stratagems, and afterward go forth.
translations.idiomatic: They hold the choke points; our men are rattled. We must steady them, lay fresh stratagems, then move.

sentences.zh: 今便示退，賊當謂吾怖，仍來相蹙，必敗之勢也。

translations.literal: If now we immediately show withdrawal, the bandits will suppose we fear and will come again to press us—it is the posture of certain defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Show weakness now and they will think us frightened and close in—we would invite defeat.

sentences.zh: 」乃密與瑾立計，令瑾督舟船，遜悉上兵馬，以向襄陽城。

translations.literal: " He then secretly with Jin established a plan, ordering Jin to supervise boats and ships; Xun brought up all infantry and cavalry toward Xiangyang city.
translations.idiomatic: He confided a plan to Jin: Jin would hold the fleet while Xun marched every soldier toward Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 敵素憚遜，遽還赴城。

translations.literal: The enemy has always feared Xun; they hurried back to man the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei troops, who dreaded Xun, rushed back to defend the walls.

sentences.zh: 瑾便引船出，遜徐整部伍，張拓聲勢，步趨船，敵不敢干。

translations.literal: Jin then led the boats out; Xun slowly reorganized the formations, spread and expanded sound and momentum, foot hastened to the boats; the enemy did not dare oppose.
translations.idiomatic: Jin slipped the fleet downstream while Xun re-formed his ranks with a show of force and marched the infantry aboard unopposed.

sentences.zh: 軍到白圍，託言住獵，潛遣將軍周峻、張梁等擊江夏新市、安陸、石陽，石陽市盛，峻等奄至，人皆捐物入城。

translations.literal: When the army reached Baiwei, they pretended to say they were stopping to hunt; secretly they dispatched Generals Zhou Jun, Zhang Liang, and others to strike Jiangxia's Xinshi, Anlu, and Shiyang; Shiyang's market was flourishing; Jun and others suddenly arrived; people all cast aside goods and entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Baiwei they announced a hunting halt while Zhou Jun and Zhang Liang swept down on Xinshi, Anlu, and bustling Shiyang in Jiangxia. The townsfolk abandoned their bundles at the gates.

sentences.zh: 城門噎不得關，敵乃自斫殺己民。

translations.literal: The city gates choked and could not be closed; the enemy then themselves hacked and killed their own people.
translations.idiomatic: The crush blocked the gates; defenders slew their own people to shut them.

sentences.zh: 然後得闔。

translations.literal: Only afterward could they close.
translations.idiomatic: Only then could they bar the doors.

sentences.zh: 斬首獲生，凡千餘人。

translations.literal: Beheadings and captures alive amounted altogether to over a thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: They killed or captured more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以为逊虑孙权以退，魏得专力於己，既能张拓形势，使敌不敢犯，方舟顺流，无复怵惕矣，何为复潜遣诸将，奄袭小县，致令市人骇奔，自相伤害？

translations.literal: Your subject Pei Songzhi thought: Xun considered that with Sun Quan's withdrawal, Wei could concentrate force on him; since he was already able to expand the situation and make the enemy not dare offend, with boats in a line going with the current, there was no more fear and trembling—why again secretly dispatch the various generals, suddenly raid small counties, causing market people to panic and flee, mutually harming one another?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi objected: If Xun reasoned that Wei's return east freed Cao Wei to focus on him, and he had already bluffed the enemy into caution and could float downstream unthreatened, why then launch secret raids on petty towns, panicking commoners into trampling one another?

sentences.zh: 俘馘千人，未足损魏，徒使无辜之民横罹荼酷，与诸葛渭滨之师，何其殊哉！

translations.literal: Captives and severed ears a thousand men—not enough to harm Wei, vainly causing innocent people to suffer bitter cruelty in the crossways—compared with Zhuge's army on the Wei River bank, how different they are!
translations.idiomatic: A thousand prisoners hardly hurt Wei; they only made blameless townsfolk suffer. How far this is from Zhuge Liang's measured host on the Wei!

sentences.zh: 用兵之道既违，失律之凶宜应，其祚无三世，及孙而灭，岂此之餘殃哉！〉

translations.literal: The way of using troops having been violated, the ill omen of losing regulation ought to answer; their fortune has not three generations; reaching the grandsons it is destroyed—is it not the residue bane of this!
translations.idiomatic: When warmaking breaks the art of war, the penalty follows. Wu's line did not last three generations—perished in the grandson's reign—perhaps this was one seed of that end."

sentences.zh: 其所生得，皆加營護，不令兵士千擾侵侮。

translations.literal: All whom they took alive, he added encampment protection, not allowing soldiers to disturb, encroach, or insult.
translations.idiomatic: Every prisoner was sheltered; troops were forbidden to molest them.

sentences.zh: 將家屬來者，使就料視。

translations.literal: Those who brought wives and children, he caused to go for inspection and viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Families who came forward were examined and registered.

sentences.zh: 若亡其妻子者，即給衣糧，厚加慰勞，發遺令還，或有感慕相攜而歸者。

translations.literal: If they had lost their wives and children, he then supplied clothing and grain, thickly added consolation and labor, sent off ordering them to return, or some felt gratitude and admiration and together carried one another back.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone separated from kin received clothing, food, and kind words before being sent home; some, moved by his decency, brought neighbors back with them.

sentences.zh: 鄰境懷之，

translations.literal: The neighboring borders cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: The borderlands remembered him warmly.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以为此无异残林覆巢而全其遗{壳鸟}，曲惠小仁，何补大虐？〉

translations.literal: Your subject Pei Songzhi thought that this was no different from wrecking the woods and overturning the nest yet sparing the fledglings left behind—a twisted minor kindness; how does it remedy great cruelty?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi commented that this was like burning the woods and ruining the nest while sparing a few chicks—petty mercy that cannot undo wholesale harm.

sentences.zh: 江夏功曹趙濯、弋陽備將裴生及夷王梅頤等，並帥支黨來附遜。

translations.literal: The Jiangxia clerk Zhao Zhuo, Yiyang reserve officer Pei Sheng, and the Yi king Mei Yi and others together led their branches and factions to come attach to Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhuo of Jiangxia, Pei Sheng from Yiyang, tribal king Mei Yi, and their followers all pledged themselves to Xun.

sentences.zh: 遜傾財帛，周贍經恤。

translations.literal: Xun poured out wealth and silk, universally aiding and relieving.
translations.idiomatic: Xun spent his own treasure to feed and comfort them.

sentences.zh: 又魏江夏太守逮式

translations.literal: Moreover Wei's Administrator of Jiangxia, Lu Shi (main text writes the surname 逮; note identifies 逯)
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wei's Jiangxia prefect Lu Shi—sources disagree on the orthography of his surname.

sentences.zh: 〈逯立录。〉

translations.literal: The Lu family register notes the name as Lu (逯) for the character written 逮.
translations.idiomatic: A sidebar records the name as Lu Shi—the main text uses a different character for the surname.

sentences.zh: 兼領兵馬，頗作邊害。

translations.literal: also commanded troops and horses and rather caused border harm.
translations.idiomatic: He also commanded troops and became a nuisance on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 而與北舊將文聘子休宿不協。

translations.literal: But with the northern old general Wen Pin's son Xiu he had long been incompatible.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been at odds with Wen Pin's son Wen Xiu, the northern veteran.

sentences.zh: 遜聞其然。

translations.literal: Xun heard it was so.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun learned of it,

sentences.zh: 即假作答式書云：「得報懇惻，知與休久結嫌隙，勢不兩存，欲來歸附，輒以密呈來書表聞，撰眾相迎。

translations.literal: he at once forged a reply letter to Shi saying: "Having received your report earnest and sincere, I know that with Xiu you long ago tied resentment and rift; the situation allows two not to survive; you wish to come and attach—I then secretly presented your incoming letter to memorialize and hear, gathered masses to welcome.
translations.idiomatic: he forged a letter to Dai Shi: "Your heartfelt plea is understood—you and Wen Xiu cannot coexist; you wish to defect. I have secretly forwarded your letter to the throne and am gathering troops to welcome you.

sentences.zh: 宜潛速嚴，更示定期。

translations.literal: You ought secretly and swiftly to prepare rigorously; further show a fixed date.
translations.idiomatic: Prepare in secret and send a firm rendezvous."

sentences.zh: 」以書置界上，式兵得書以見式，式惶懼，遂自送妻子還洛。

translations.literal: " He placed the letter on the border; Shi's troops obtained the letter and showed Shi; Shi was fearful and alarmed; thereupon himself escorted wife and children back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He planted the letter on the border. Dai's men showed it to him; panic-stricken, Dai sent his family to Luoyang himself.

sentences.zh: 由是史士不復親附，遂以免罷。

translations.literal: Thereby clerks and soldiers no longer personally attached; thereupon he was dismissed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: His officers deserted him and he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松以为边将为害，盖其常事，使逯式得罪，代者亦复如之，自非狡焉思肆，将成大患，何足亏损雅虑，尚为小诈哉？

translations.literal: Your subject Pei Songzhi thought that border generals causing harm is generally their constant affair; if Lu Shi is made to offend, his replacement will again be like this—unless he is cunning and plots license and will become a great calamity—what suffices to damage refined planning, still to employ petty deceit?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi argued that frontier officers often make trouble; removing Dai Shi only replaces one headache with another unless the man is truly dangerous—hardly worth sullying high policy with a petty ruse.

sentences.zh: 以斯为美，又所不取。〉

translations.literal: To take this as beautiful is again what I do not accept."
translations.idiomatic: Calling such deceit admirable is something I reject."

sentences.zh: 六年，中郎將周祗乞於鄱陽召募，事下問遜。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, General of the Household Zhou Qi begged to recruit in Poyang; the matter was sent down to ask Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chiwu (243 CE), General Zhou Qi asked to levy troops in Poyang; the court referred the matter to Xun.

sentences.zh: 遜以為此郡民易動難安，不可與召。

translations.literal: Xun believed this commandery's people were easy to stir and hard to pacify; one could not grant recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Xun argued that Poyang's people were volatile—recruitment would be unwise.

sentences.zh: 恐致賊寇。

translations.literal: He feared it would bring bandit raiders.
translations.idiomatic: It would spark rebellion.

sentences.zh: 而祗固陳取之，郡民吳遽等果作賊殺祗，攻沒諸縣。

translations.literal: But Qi firmly insisted on taking them; commandery commoners Wu Ju and others indeed acted as bandits, killed Qi, and attacked and overwhelmed the various counties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi insisted; Wu Ju of the county rose in revolt, slew Zhou Qi, and overran the districts.

sentences.zh: 豫章、廬陵宿惡民並應遽為寇。

translations.literal: Yuzhang and Luling longstanding wicked commoners together responded to Ju and became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hardened malcontents in Yuzhang and Luling joined Wu Ju's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 遜自聞，輒討即破，遽等相率降，遜料得精兵八千餘人，三郡平。

translations.literal: When Xun himself heard, he at once campaigned and broke them; Ju and others led one another to surrender; Xun selected and obtained crack troops over eight thousand persons; three commanderies were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xun marched as soon as word reached him, crushed the rising, and accepted Wu Ju's surrender. He drafted eight thousand elite soldiers and pacified three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 時中書典校呂壹，竊弄權柄，擅作威福。

translations.literal: At that time the Palace Documents inspector Lü Yi secretly played with power's handle and presumptuously exercised awe and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Palace inspector Lü Yi had seized clandestine power and threw his weight around.

sentences.zh: 遜與太常潘浚同心憂之，言至流涕。

translations.literal: Xun together with the Chamberlain Pan Jun with one heart worried over it; speaking reached shedding tears.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Chamberlain Pan Jun agonized together until they wept.

sentences.zh: 後權誅壹，深以自責，語在《權傳》。

translations.literal: Later Quan executed Yi and deeply blamed himself—the words are in Quan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan later executed Lü Yi and bitterly blamed himself; see Sun Quan's biography.

sentences.zh: 時謝淵、謝厷等各陳便宜，欲興利改作，

translations.literal: At that time Xie Yuan, Xie Gong, and others each presented what was expedient, wishing to raise profit and alter works,
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yuan, Xie Gong, and others petitioned with proposals for reform and profit,

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：谢渊字休德，少修德操，躬秉耒耜，既无慼容，又不易虑，由是知名。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji Canon Record states: Xie Yuan, courtesy name Xiude, in youth cultivated virtue and integrity; personally grasped plow and hoe; had neither sorrowful expression nor altered worries; thereby became known.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji Canon Record says Xie Yuan, styled Xiude, farmed his own fields without complaint or distraction and won a reputation.

sentences.zh: 举孝廉，稍迁至建武将军，虽在戎旅，犹垂意人物。

translations.literal: He was recommended filial and incorrupt; gradually promoted until General Who Establishes Might; although in military camp, still bent mind on men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he rose to General Who Establishes Might and still championed worthy men even on campaign.

sentences.zh: 骆统子名秀，被门庭之谤，众论狐疑，莫能证明。

translations.literal: Luo Tong's son named Xiu suffered slander at the gate; crowd opinion was doubtful; none could verify.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tong's son Xiu faced nasty gossip at home; rumor wavered and no one could clear him.

sentences.zh: 渊闻之叹息曰：「公绪早夭，同盟所哀。

translations.literal: When Yuan heard it he sighed and said: "Gongxu died young—it is what allies mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sighed: "Gongxu died young—we who swore fellowship still grieve.

sentences.zh: 闻其子志行明辩，而被闇昧之谤，望诸夫子烈然高断，而各怀迟疑，非所望也。

translations.literal: I hear his son's aims and conduct are clear and discriminating, yet he suffers slander of dark obscurity—I hoped you gentlemen would fiercely and loftily decide, yet each harbors hesitation—not what was hoped.
translations.idiomatic: His son's character is bright enough, yet murky slander clings—I hoped you elders would judge decisively; instead you hesitate—that falls short of what I expected.

sentences.zh: 」秀卒见明，无复瑕玷，终为显士，渊之力也。

translations.literal: " Xiu in the end was seen clearly; no further flaw or stain; in the end became an eminent gentleman—it was Yuan's effort.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was vindicated, cleared of stain, and rose to distinction—thanks to Yuan's advocacy."

sentences.zh: 吴历称云，谢厷才辩有计术。〉

translations.literal: The Wu Calendar praises him, saying Xie Gong was talented in debate and had stratagem and method.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Calendar praises Xie Gong's eloquence and craft."

sentences.zh: 以事下遜。

translations.literal: On the matter it was sent down to Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The proposals went to Xun for review.

sentences.zh: 遜議曰：

translations.literal: Xun deliberated saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xun replied:

sentences.zh: 國以民為本，強由民力，財由民出。

translations.literal: The state takes the people as root; strength comes from the people's power; wealth comes from the people's outlay.
translations.idiomatic: The state rests on the people—its strength and wealth rise from them.

sentences.zh: 夫民殷國弱，民瘠國強者，末之有也。

translations.literal: As for the people thriving yet the state weak, or the people exhausted yet the state strong—never has such been.
translations.idiomatic: The people and the throne rise or fall together—prosperous subjects do not pair with a broken dynasty, nor desperate subjects with a vigorous one.

sentences.zh: 故為國者，得民則治，失之則亂，若不受利，而令盡用立效，亦為難也。

translations.literal: Therefore those who govern the state, obtaining the people then order, losing them then chaos; if they do not receive benefit yet order them to exhaust use and establish effect—this too is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Thus whoever wins the people governs well; whoever loses them faces chaos. Demanding full exertion without granting gain is futile.

sentences.zh: 是以《詩》歎‘宜民宜人，受祿於天’。

translations.literal: Therefore the Classic of Poetry sighs 'fitting the people, fitting men—receiving blessing from heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry praises rulers who suit both people and nobles and receive heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 乞垂聖恩，寧濟百姓，數年之間，國用少豐，然後更圖。

translations.literal: I beg to let sagely grace descend, tranquilly succor the hundred surnames; within several years state use will be somewhat abundant; afterward plan again.
translations.idiomatic: Extend mercy, steady the commoners, fill the treasury in a few years, then revisit reform."

sentences.zh: 赤烏七年，代顧雍丞相，詔曰：

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chiwu, he replaced Gu Yong as chancellor; an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In Chiwu 7 (244 CE) he succeeded Gu Yong as chancellor. The edict read:

sentences.zh: 朕以不德。

translations.literal: We, lacking virtue.
translations.idiomatic: We lack virtue,

sentences.zh: 應其踐運，王塗未一，奸宄充路，夙夜戰懼，不遑鑒寐。

translations.literal: responding to treading the mandate, the king's path is not yet one; wickedness fills the roads; morning and evening we tremble in fear; no leisure for polished sleep.
translations.idiomatic: yet heaven called us to rule while the realm stays divided and villains throng the roads. We tremble day and night and scarcely sleep.

sentences.zh: 惟君天資聰睿，明德顯融，統任上將，匡國彌難。

translations.literal: Only you, heaven-bestowed intelligence and keen insight, bright virtue manifestly harmonious, united appointment as senior general, aiding the state in filling hardship.
translations.idiomatic: You combine keen judgment with luminous virtue; as commander-in-chief you have steadied the state through crisis.

sentences.zh: 夫有超世之功者，必應光大之寵；

translations.literal: As for those who have merit surpassing the age, they must correspond to brilliant great favor;
translations.idiomatic: Those who surpass their age deserve surpassing honor;

sentences.zh: 懷文武之者，必荷社稷之重。

translations.literal: those who harbor civil and martial talents must bear the altars of soil and grain's heavy burden.
translations.idiomatic: those who unite civil and martial gifts must shoulder the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 昔伊尹隆湯，呂尚翼周，內外之任，君實兼之。

translations.literal: Formerly Yi Yin elevated Tang, Lü Shang winged Zhou—inner and outer duties—you truly combine them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin raised Shang; Lü Wang aided Zhou—you bear both inner and outer charge as they did.

sentences.zh: 今以君為丞相，使使持節守太常傅常授印綬。

translations.literal: Now We appoint you chancellor, dispatching the bearer of credentials, Guardian Chamberlain Fu Chang, to confer seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: We name you chancellor and send Fu Chang of the Chamberlain's office with the seals of office.

sentences.zh: 君其茂昭明德，修乃懿績，敬服王命，綏靖四方。

translations.literal: You ought splendidly display bright virtue, cultivate your fine accomplishments, reverently submit to kingly commands, pacify and quiet the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Brighten your virtue, perfect your record, obey the throne's commands, and bring peace to the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 於乎！

translations.literal: Oh!
translations.idiomatic: Ah!

sentences.zh: 總司三事，以訓群寮，可不敬歟，君其勖之!其州牧都護領武昌事如故。

translations.literal: Overall oversee the three affairs, thereby instruct the host of officials—can you not be reverent! You ought encourage yourself! Your governorship, protector-generalship, and charge of Wuchang affairs remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: You oversee the Three Offices and instruct the bureaucracy—approach this with awe and strive still harder. You remain Governor, Protector-General, and governor of Wuchang as before."

sentences.zh: 先是，二宮並闕，中外職司，多遣子弟給侍。

translations.literal: Before this, the two palaces both had vacancies; inner and outer office-holders for the most part sent sons and younger brothers to attend and serve.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, with both Heir and Prince of Lu building factions, officials at court and in the provinces sent sons to staff the two households.

sentences.zh: 全琮報遜，遜以為“子弟苟有才，不憂不用，不宜私出以要榮利。

translations.literal: Quan Zong reported to Xun; Xun held that "if sons and younger brothers have talent, one need not worry they will not be used; it is not fitting privately to go out to seek glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong informed Xun, who wrote: "If your sons are truly able, they will be employed in due course; they should not angle for position in the princes' courts.

sentences.zh: 若其不佳，終為取禍。

translations.literal: If they are not good, in the end it will bring obtaining disaster.
