translations.idiomatic: If they are not, they will only court disaster.

sentences.zh: 且聞二宮勢敵，必有彼此，此古人之厚忌也。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear the two palaces' forces are matched; there must be this one and that one—this is what the ancients deeply shunned.
translations.idiomatic: The two establishments are at odds—ancient sages most feared that.

sentences.zh: ”琮子寄，果阿附魯王，輕為交構。

translations.literal: " Zong's son Ji indeed fawned and attached to the Prince of Lu, lightly making entanglements.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's son Ji toadied to the Prince of Lu and stirred trouble anyway.

sentences.zh: 遜書與琮曰：「卿不師日磾，而宿留阿寄，終為足下門戶致禍矣。

translations.literal: Xun wrote to Zong saying: "You do not model yourself on Rizhi, yet long detain A Ji—in the end it will for your foot bring calamity to gate and door.
translations.idiomatic: Xun wrote: "You do not imitate Jin Midi's stern virtue yet harbor Ji—you will bring ruin on your house.

sentences.zh: 」琮既不納，更以致隙。

translations.literal: " Zong neither accepted; moreover thereby caused rift.
translations.idiomatic: Zong ignored him, and their friendship cooled.

sentences.zh: 及太子有不安之儀，遜上疏陳：「太子正統，宜有磐石之固，魯王藩臣，當使寵秩有差，彼此得所，上下獲安。

translations.literal: When the heir had unsettled demeanor, Xun submitted a memorial stating: "The heir is orthodox succession; he ought to have firmness like bedrock; the Prince of Lu is a feudatory minister—one ought to make favor and rank have differences; each side obtains its place; above and below obtain peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince looked insecure, Xun memorialized: "The heir holds the legitimate line and must stand immovable as rock; the Prince of Lu is only a feudatory prince—rank and favor must differ so both houses and the throne stay secure.

sentences.zh: 謹叩頭流血以聞。

translations.literal: I respectfully knock head bleeding to report.
translations.idiomatic: I kowtow until blood flows to make this heard."

sentences.zh: 」書三四上，及求詣都，欲口論適庶之分，以匡得失。

translations.literal: " The letters three or four went up, and he sought to go to the capital, wishing orally to discuss legitimate versus secondary distinction, thereby correcting gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: He sent three or four memorials and asked leave to come to the capital to argue the heir's status in person.

sentences.zh: 既不聽許，而遜外生顧譚、顧承、姚信，工以親附太子，枉見流徙。

translations.literal: Since permission was not granted, yet Xun's sister's sons Gu Tan, Gu Cheng, and Yao Xin, because they together by kinship attached to the heir, were wrongly seen banished and exiled.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan refused. Xun's nephews Gu Tan, Gu Cheng, and Yao Xin, who had sided with the heir through family ties, were unjustly banished.

sentences.zh: 太子太傅吾粲坐數與遜交書，下獄死。

translations.literal: The heir's senior tutor Wu Can sat because of repeatedly exchanging letters with Xun; was cast into prison and died.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's tutor Wu Can was jailed and died for frequently corresponding with Xun.

sentences.zh: 權累遣中使責讓遜，遜憤恚致卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: Quan repeatedly dispatched inner envoys to blame and reproach Xun; Xun in resentful anger brought about death; at the time age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan repeatedly sent envoys to upbraid him. Xun died of rage and grief at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 家無餘財。

translations.literal: The house had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He left no fortune behind.

sentences.zh: 初，暨艷造營府之論，遜諫戒之，以為必禍。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Ji Yan created the camp headquarters theory; Xun remonstrated and warned him, holding it would surely bring calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji Yan floated his scheme to rank officers, Xun warned him it would end in disaster.

sentences.zh: 又謂諸葛恪曰：「在我前者，吾必奉之同升；

translations.literal: He also said to Zhuge Ke: "Those before me, I must serve them to rise together;
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhuge Ke: "Those senior to me I will raise alongside myself;

sentences.zh: 在我下者，則扶持之。

translations.literal: those below me, then I support and uphold them.
translations.idiomatic: those junior I will lift up.

sentences.zh: 今觀君氣陵其上，意蔑乎下。

translations.literal: Now observing you, your qi overrides those above; your intent despises those below.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you lord it over your superiors and despise those beneath.

sentences.zh: 非安德之基也。

translations.literal: This is not the foundation for securing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: That is no way to build lasting safety."

sentences.zh: 」又廣陵楊竺少獲聲名，而遜謂之終敗。

translations.literal: " Moreover Guangling Yang Zhu in youth obtained reputation, yet Xun called him in the end defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhu of Guangling rose young to fame, yet Xun predicted his ruin.

sentences.zh: 勸竺兄穆令與別族。

translations.literal: He urged Zhu's elder brother Mu to order separation of lineage.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Zhu's brother Mu to split the clan and distance himself.

sentences.zh: 其先睹如此。

translations.literal: His foresight was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his foresight.

sentences.zh: 長子延早夭，次子抗襲爵。

translations.literal: The eldest son Yan died young; the second son Kang inherited the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yan died young; the second, Kang, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 孫休時，追謚遜曰昭侯。

translations.literal: At Sun Xiu's time, posthumously titled Xun Marquis Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Xiu he was posthumously titled Marquis Zhao.

sentences.zh: 抗字幼節，孫策外孫也。

translations.literal: Kang, courtesy name Youjie, was Sun Ce's maternal grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang, styled Youjie, was a grandson of Sun Ce on the distaff side.

sentences.zh: 遜卒時，年二十，拜建武校尉，領遜眾五千人，送葬東還，詣都謝恩，孫權以楊竺所白遜二十事問抗，禁絕賓客，中使臨詰，抗無所顧問，事事條答，權意漸解。

translations.literal: When Xun died, he was twenty years old; he was appointed Colonel Who Establishes Might, leading Xun's host of five thousand men; he escorted the funeral east returning, went to the capital to thank grace; Quan with what Yang Zhu had denounced in twenty items concerning Xun questioned Kang; he cut off guests and clients; inner envoys came to interrogate; Kang had no one to consult with; item by item he answered in order; Quan's intent gradually relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was twenty when his father died. He became Colonel Who Establishes Might with five thousand of Xun's troops, escorted the bier east, then went to the capital. Sun Quan, acting on Yang Zhu's twenty counts against Xun, isolated Kang and sent eunuchs to question him. Kang needed no brief—he answered each charge from memory until Sun Quan's anger eased.

sentences.zh: 赤烏九年，遷立節中郎將，與諸葛恪換屯柴桑。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chiwu, he was promoted General of the Household Who Establishes Integrity and exchanged garrison with Zhuge Ke at Chaisang.
translations.idiomatic: In Chiwu 9 (246 CE) he rose to General of the Household Who Establishes Integrity and swapped bases with Zhuge Ke at Chaisang.

sentences.zh: 抗臨去，皆更繕完城圍，葺其牆屋，居廬桑果，不得妄敗。

translations.literal: When Kang was about to depart, he everywhere anew repaired and completed city ramparts, thatched their walls and houses; dwellings, huts, mulberries, and fruits—none might wantonly ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he rebuilt walls and roofs and forbade any damage to houses, mulberries, or orchards.

sentences.zh: 恪入屯，儼然若新。

translations.literal: When Ke entered garrison, it was solemn as if new.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Ke took over, the camp looked newly built.

sentences.zh: 而恪柴桑故屯，頗有毀壞，深以為慚。

translations.literal: But Ke's old Chaisang garrison had considerable ruin and destruction; he deeply took it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke felt ashamed that his old Chaisang post lay half ruined.

sentences.zh: 太元元年，就都治病。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiyuan, he went to the capital for treating illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan 1 (251 CE) he went to the capital for medical care.

sentences.zh: 病差當還。

translations.literal: When illness improved he ought return.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered he prepared to return.

sentences.zh: 權涕泣與別，謂曰：「吾前聽用讒言，與汝父大義不篤，以此負汝。

translations.literal: Quan wept tears parting with him, saying to him: "I formerly listened to and employed slanderous words; with your father great righteousness was not sincere—thereby I wronged you.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wept at leave-taking: "I once listened to slander and wronged your father—that wrong rests on you.

sentences.zh: 前後所問，一焚滅之，莫令人見也。

translations.literal: What was questioned before and after, altogether burn and destroy it—do not order people to see.
translations.idiomatic: Burn every accusation lodged against him—let no one see them again."

sentences.zh: 」建興元年，拜奮威將軍。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Jianxing, he was appointed General Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 (252 CE) he became General Who Displays Might.

sentences.zh: 太平二年，魏將諸葛誕舉壽春降，拜抗為柴桑督，赴壽春，破魏牙門將偏將軍，遷征北將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping, Wei general Zhuge Dan raised Shouchun to surrender; Kang was appointed Chaisang commander, went to Shouchun, defeated Wei's camp-gate general and lieutenant-general, was promoted General Who Conquers the North.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping 2 (257 CE), when Zhuge Dan surrendered Shouchun, Kang took command at Chaisang, marched to Shouchun, routed Wei's camp officers, and rose to General Who Conquers the North.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，拜鎮軍將軍，都督西陵，自關羽至白帝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an, he was appointed General Who Guards the Army, area commander of Xiling, from the Guan Yu defense line to Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an 2 (259 CE) he became General Who Guards the Army with river defense responsibility from the old Guan Yu sector to Baidi.

sentences.zh: 三年，假節。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was lent credentials.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he received imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 孫皓即位，加鎮軍大將軍，領益州牧。

translations.literal: When Sun Hao assumed the throne, he was added Grand General Who Guards the Army, concurrent Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao promoted him to Grand General Who Guards the Army with nominal tenure as Governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 建衡二年，左大司馬施績卒，拜抗都督信陵、西陵、夷道、樂鄉、公安諸軍事，治樂鄉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianheng, Left Grand Marshal Shi Ji died; Kang was appointed area commander of Xinling, Xiling, Yidao, Lexiang, Gong'an military affairs, administering Lexiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Grand Marshal Shi Ji died in Jianheng 2 (270 CE), Kang took overall command from Xinling through Gong'an with headquarters at Lexiang.

sentences.zh: 抗聞都下政令多闕，憂深慮遠。

translations.literal: When Kang heard the capital below had many gaps in government commands, his worry was deep and consideration far.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing endless flaws in court policy, Kang grew deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He therefore memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣聞德均則眾者勝寡，力侔則安者制危，蓋六國所以兼併於強秦，西楚所以北面於漢高也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that when virtue is equal then the many defeat the few; when strength is matched then the secure control the perilous—this is why the six states were annexed by powerful Qin and why Western Chu faced north toward Han Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: When virtue is evenly matched, numbers decide the fight; when strength is comparable, the steadier hand wins—how the six states fell to Qin and Xiang Yu bowed to Liu Bang.

sentences.zh: 今敵跨制九服，非徒關右之地。

translations.literal: Now the enemy strides controlling the nine domains—not merely the lands west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Wei spans the nine provinces—not merely Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 割據九州，豈但鴻溝以西而已。

translations.literal: They carve and occupy the nine provinces—how can it be only west of the Hong Canal?
translations.idiomatic: They hold the nine regions—far beyond the Hong Canal line.

sentences.zh: 國家外無連國之援，內非西楚之強，庶政陵遲，黎民未乂。

translations.literal: Our state without has no allied state's aid; within we are not Western Chu's strength; various governance declines and slackens; black-haired people are not governed.
translations.idiomatic: We lack allies abroad and strength at home like Western Chu; administration slackens and the people lack peace.

sentences.zh: 而議者所恃，徒以長川峻山，限帶封域，此乃守國之末事，非智者之所先也。

translations.literal: Yet what debaters rely on is solely long rivers and steep mountains, belt-limiting sealed territory—this is guarding the state's least affair, not what wise men put first.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors trust only rivers and mountains—that is the last resort of defense, not what wise rulers prioritize.

sentences.zh: 臣每遠惟戰國存亡之符，近覽劉氏傾覆之釁，考之曲籍，驗之行事，中夜撫枕，臨餐忘食。

translations.literal: Your subject often from afar ponders the Warring States' survival and perdition signs; from near surveys the Liu clan's overturning omens; examines them in bent records; verifies them in conducted affairs; midnight strokes the pillow; facing meal forgets food.
translations.idiomatic: I study Warring States fate and Han's fall in the texts, then watch our own conduct—I wake at midnight clutching my pillow and lose my appetite.

sentences.zh: 昔匈奴未滅，去病辭館。

translations.literal: Formerly when the Xiongnu were not yet destroyed, Qubing declined mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Qubing refused mansions while the Xiongnu lived.

sentences.zh: 漢道未純，賈生哀泣，況臣王室之出，世荷光寵，身名否泰，與國同戚，死生契闊，義無苟且，夙夜憂怛，念至情慘。

translations.literal: Han doctrine was not yet pure; Jia Sheng wept in sorrow—moreover your subject is of royal house extraction; generations bear bright favor; body and name rise or fall; with the state share sorrow; death and life bind or part—righteousness permits no carelessness; morning and evening anxious and distressed; when thoughts arrive the feeling is tragic.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi wept while Han still wandered from the Way—I spring from the imperial clan, owe everything to the throne, rise or fall with Wu, share life and death with it. Duty forbids complacency; grief keeps me sleepless.

sentences.zh: 夫事君之義犯而勿欺，人臣之節匪躬是殉，謹陳時宜十七條如左。

translations.literal: As for serving the lord's righteousness—offend yet do not deceive; as for minister's integrity—not self but martyrdom—I respectfully present timely affairs seventeen articles as at left.
translations.idiomatic: A loyal minister may risk offense but never deceit; he stakes life on duty. I therefore submit seventeen timely proposals below."

sentences.zh: 十七條失本，故不載。

translations.literal: The seventeen articles have lost their originals; therefore they are not carried.
translations.idiomatic: The seventeen proposals no longer survive in the sources and are omitted.

sentences.zh: 時何定弄權，閹官預政。

translations.literal: At that time He Ding manipulated power; eunuchs interfered in government.
translations.idiomatic: He Ding dominated the court while eunuchs meddled in policy.

sentences.zh: 抗上疏曰：

translations.literal: Kang submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣聞開國承家，小人勿用，靖譖庸回，唐書攸戒，是以雅人所以怨刺，仲尼所以歎息也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that founding a state and continuing a family—petty men must not be employed; quieting slander and worthless associates—the Tang documents thereby warn; therefore refined men lament in criticism and Zhongni sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Founding a house forbids employing petty men—the classics warn against slanderous courtiers; poets rail against them and Confucius sighed over them.

sentences.zh: 春秋已來，爰及秦、漢，傾覆之釁，未有不由斯者也。

translations.literal: From Spring and Autumn onward, extending to Qin and Han, the omens of overturn and ruin—there has never been one not arising from this.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Spring and Autumn annals, through Qin and Han, every collapse traces back to this mistake.

sentences.zh: 小人不明理道，所見既淺，雖使竭情盡節，猶不足任，況其奸心素篤，而憎愛移易哉？

translations.literal: Petty men do not understand principle and the Way; what they see is already shallow—even if made to exhaust feeling and fulfill integrity, still insufficient to be entrusted—moreover when treacherous hearts are innately deep and love and hate shift?
translations.idiomatic: Petty men lack judgment; even at their loyal best they are unreliable—let alone when ambition runs deep and shifts with every whim.

sentences.zh: 苟患失之，無所不至。

translations.literal: If they fear losing it, there is nothing they will not reach to.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the loss of place, they stop at nothing.

sentences.zh: 今委以聰明之任，假以專制之威，而冀雍熙之聲作，肅清之化立，不可得也。

translations.literal: Now entrusting them with discerning duties and lending them sole-rule awesomeness, yet hoping for the sound of harmonious brilliance to arise and cleansing transformation to stand—cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Give them power and expect enlightened rule—impossible.

sentences.zh: 方今見吏，殊才雖少，然或冠冕之冑，少漸道孝；

translations.literal: Among officers now seen, extraordinary talent though scarce, yet some are cap-and-girdle heirs who from youth were steeped in the Way and filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: Today's officials include few stars, yet many are gentle-born and trained in duty from childhood;

sentences.zh: 或清苦自立，資能足用。

translations.literal: some through hardship stand self-established; endowment and ability suffice for employment.
translations.idiomatic: others rose through austere integrity with proven competence.

sentences.zh: 自可隨才授職，抑黜群小，然後俗化可清，庶政無穢也。

translations.literal: Naturally one may according to talent confer office, suppress and dismiss the swarm of petty men—afterward custom and transformation can be purified and various governance without filth.
translations.idiomatic: Match men to posts, purge the court of parasites, and government runs clean.

sentences.zh: 晉巴東監軍徐胤率水軍詣建平，荊州刺史楊肇至西陵。

translations.literal: Jin's Supervisor of Badong Xu Yin led the navy toward Jianping; Inspector of Jingzhou Yang Zhao arrived at Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's Xu Yin sailed toward Jianping while Jingzhou Inspector Yang Zhao reached Xiling.

sentences.zh: 抗令張咸固守其城；

translations.literal: Kang ordered Zhang Xian firmly to guard that city;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang ordered Zhang Xian to hold the walls;

sentences.zh: 公安督孫遵巡南岸御祜；

translations.literal: the Gong'an commander Sun Zun patrolled the south bank to oppose Hu;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zun of Gong'an patrolled the south shore against Yang Hu;

sentences.zh: 水軍督留慮、鎮西將軍朱琬拒胤。

translations.literal: Navy commander Liu Lü and General Who Guards the West Zhu Wan opposed Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lü and Zhu Wan blocked Xu Yin.

sentences.zh: 身率三軍，憑圍對肇。

translations.literal: He personally led the three armies, relying on the siege works to face Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang led the host from behind the siege lines against Yang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 將軍朱喬、營都督俞贊亡詣肇。

translations.literal: General Zhu Qiao and camp commander Yu Zan defected to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qiao and Yu Zan deserted to Yang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 抗曰：「贊軍中舊吏，知吾虛實者，吾常慮夷兵素不簡練，若敵攻圍，必先此處。

translations.literal: Kang said: "Zan was an old clerk in the army—one who knows our emptiness and fullness—I always worried that Yi troops have never been picked and drilled; if the enemy attacks the siege, they will surely strike this place first.
translations.idiomatic: Kang said: "Yu Zan knows our order of battle. I always feared our tribal auxiliaries were raw—the enemy would strike there first in a siege.

sentences.zh: 」即夜易夷民，皆以舊將充之。

translations.literal: " That night he exchanged Yi foot soldiers—all filled with veteran generals.
translations.idiomatic: That night he swapped the tribal levies for seasoned officers.

sentences.zh: 明日，肇果攻故夷兵處，抗命旋軍擊之，矢石雨下，肇眾傷死者相屬。

translations.literal: Next day Zhao indeed attacked the former Yi troop position; Kang ordered wheeling armies to strike them; arrows and stones rained down; Zhao's host wounded and dead linked one to another.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning Zhao hit the old tribal sector; Kang wheeled his line and crushed him under a storm of missiles.

sentences.zh: 肇至經月。

translations.literal: Zhao arrived passing a month.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhao had been there a full month.

sentences.zh: 計屈夜遁。

translations.literal: Plans exhausted, by night he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Out of options, he slipped away by night.

sentences.zh: 抗欲追之，而慮闡畜力項領，伺視間隙，兵不足分，於是但鳴鼓戒眾，若將追者。

translations.literal: Kang wished to pursue them, yet worried Chan stored strength at neck and throat, watched for gaps and openings; troops were insufficient to divide—thereupon only beat drums warning the masses as if about to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Kang wanted pursuit but feared Bu Chan held fresh troops in reserve; his own men were stretched thin. He beat drums as if chasing to bluff Yang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 肇眾兇懼，悉解甲挺走，抗使輕兵躡之，肇大破敗，祜等皆引軍還。

translations.literal: Zhao's host was fierce with fear; all doffed armor and fled running; Kang sent light troops to tread on them; Zhao was greatly broken and defeated; Hu and others all led armies back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's men panicked, threw off armor, and fled; light Wu troops ran them down. Yang Zhao routed; Yang Hu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 抗遂陷西陵城，誅夷闡族及其大將吏，自此以下，所請赦者數萬口。

translations.literal: Kang thereupon took Xiling city, executed and extirpated Chan's clan and his great generals and clerks; from this downward those begged pardon numbered tens of thousands of mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Kang stormed Xiling, executed Bu Chan's clan and senior officers, and spared tens of thousands who pleaded mercy.

sentences.zh: 修治城圍，東還樂鄉，貌無矜色，謙沖如常，故得將士歡心。

translations.literal: He repaired and ordered city ramparts, returned east to Lexiang; countenance had no prideful color; humble and yielding as usual—therefore obtained generals' and soldiers' joyful hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the walls, marched east to Lexiang without swagger, and kept the army's devotion.

sentences.zh: 〈《晉陽秋》曰：抗與羊祜推僑、札之好。

translations.literal: The Jin Yangqiu states: Kang together with Yang Hu extended the friendship of Qiao and Zha.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Yangqiu records that Lu Kang and Yang Hu cultivated the diplomatic courtesy once shown between Ji Zha of Wu and Zichan of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 抗嘗遺祜酒，祜飲之不疑。

translations.literal: Kang once presented Hu wine; Hu drank it without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Kang once sent wine; Yang Hu drank without fear of poison.

sentences.zh: 抗有疾，祜饋之藥，抗亦推心服之。

translations.literal: When Kang had illness, Hu presented him medicine; Kang likewise pushed heart and trusted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang fell ill, Hu sent physic; Kang swallowed it in the same spirit of trust.

sentences.zh: 於時以為華元、子反復見於今。

translations.literal: At the time they were thought Hua Yuan and Zifan again seen in the present.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers said Hua Yuan and Sima Zifan lived again.

sentences.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：羊祜既歸，增脩德信，以懷吳人。

translations.literal: The Han Jin Annals states: after Hu returned, he increased cultivating virtue and trust to cherish Wu people.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Jin Annals adds that Yang Hu, once home, doubled down on good faith to win eastern hearts.

sentences.zh: 陸抗每告其邊戍曰：「彼專為德，我專為暴，是不戰而自服也。

translations.literal: Lu Kang often told his border garrisons: "They devote solely to virtue; we devote solely to cruelty—this is to submit without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang told the frontier: "If they brandish virtue while we brandish cruelty, we surrender without a battle.

sentences.zh: 各保分界，無求細益而已。

translations.literal: Each guards dividing boundaries; seek no petty gain—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the line and renounce petty raids—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 」於是吳、晉之間，餘糧棲畝而不犯，牛馬逸而入境，可宣告而取也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon between Wu and Jin surplus grain perched in fields yet was not violated; oxen and horses strayed and entered borders—could be announced and taken.
translations.idiomatic: Grain stood ungathered in the border belt; stray herds crossed with notice—both sides honored the truce.

sentences.zh: 沔上獵，吳獲晉人先傷者，皆送而相還。

translations.literal: Hunting on the Mian; Wu captured Jin men injured first—all sent and mutually returned.
translations.idiomatic: When hunters clashed on the Han, wounded prisoners were exchanged both ways.

sentences.zh: 抗嘗疾，求藥於祜，祜以成合與之，曰：「此上藥也，近始自作，未及服，以君疾急，故相致。

translations.literal: Kang once was ill, sought medicine from Hu; Hu with prepared doses gave him, saying: "This is superior medicine; lately I began making it myself, have not yet taken it—because your illness is urgent, therefore I send it.
translations.idiomatic: Kang once asked Hu for medicine; Hu handed over sealed doses: "I compounded this myself yesterday and have not tried it—your need is urgent, so you take it first."

sentences.zh: 」抗得而服之，諸將或諫，抗不答。

translations.literal: " Kang obtained it and took it; various generals some remonstrated; Kang did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Kang drank it despite his officers' protests and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 孫皓聞二境交和，以詰於抗，抗曰：「夫一邑一鄉，不可以無信義之人，而況大國乎？

translations.literal: When Sun Hao heard the two borders exchanged harmony, he questioned Kang; Kang said: "As for one district one village, one cannot lack men of faith and righteousness—how much more a great state?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao questioned the détente; Kang answered: "Even a hamlet needs honorable men—how much more two kingdoms?

sentences.zh: 臣不如是，正足以彰其德耳，於祜無傷也。

translations.literal: Your subject not doing thus would just suffice to display his virtue ear—it does Hu no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty gains nothing by withholding reciprocity—you only magnify Yang Hu's stature without harming him.

sentences.zh: 」或以祜、抗為失臣節，兩譏之。

translations.literal: " Some took Hu and Kang as losing ministerial integrity—both ridiculed them.
translations.idiomatic: Critics accused both men of betraying ministerial duty."

sentences.zh: ○習鑿齒曰：夫理勝者天下之所保，信順者萬人之所宗，雖大猷既喪，義聲久淪，狙詐馳於當塗，權略週乎急務，負力從橫之人，臧獲牧豎之智，未有不憑此以創功，舍茲而獨立者也。

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi says: As for principle victorious—that which the world safeguards; trust and compliance—that which ten thousand men honor. Though great plans have already perished and righteous fame long sunk, trickery races along the high road and stratagems circle urgent tasks—men who rely on force and maneuver, wisdom of slaves and herd boys—none there are who do not rely on these to establish merit; who discard this yet stand alone.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi argues that right principle and good faith win the world—even when grand strategy fails and honor fades, every conqueror from warlord to shepherd still rides on moral prestige; none thrives by sheer fraud alone.

sentences.zh: 是故晉文退舍，而原城請命；

translations.literal: Therefore Duke Wen of Jin withdrew camps—and Yuancheng begged for orders;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Jin pulled back his siege and earned Yuan's surrender;

sentences.zh: 穆子圍鼓，訓之以力；

translations.literal: Muzi surrounded Gu—instructed it with force;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Muzi stormed Gu yet taught restraint;

sentences.zh: 冶夫獻策，而費人斯歸；

translations.literal: The metallurgist presented stratagem—and Fei people thereupon returned;
translations.idiomatic: a smith's counsel brought Fei back to Lu;

sentences.zh: 樂毅緩攻，而風烈長流。

translations.literal: Yue Yi slowed attack—and fierce wind flowed long.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi's patient siege still echoes.

sentences.zh: 觀其所以服物製勝者，豈徒威力相詐而已哉！

translations.literal: Observe by what they subdue things and control victory—how can it be merely might and power mutually deceiving!
translations.idiomatic: Their victories rested on more than arms and trickery.

sentences.zh: 自今三家鼎足四十有餘年矣，吳人不能越淮、沔而進取中國，中國不能陵長江以爭利者，力均而智侔，道不足以相傾也。

translations.literal: From now the three houses tripod-footed forty-odd years; Wu men cannot cross Huai and Mian to advance and seize the Central States; the Central States cannot mount the long Yangzi to contest profit—because strength is equal and wisdom matched; the Way is insufficient mutually to overturn.
translations.idiomatic: Forty years of tripartite stalemate—neither Wu crosses the Huai and Han nor Jin masters the Long River: evenly matched strength leaves virtue the only lever.

sentences.zh: 夫殘彼而利我，未若利我而無殘；

translations.literal: As for injuring them and benefiting me—not like benefiting me without injury;
translations.idiomatic: Ravaging the foe helps us less than enriching ourselves without slaughter;

sentences.zh: 振武以懼物，未若德廣而民懷。

translations.literal: shaking martiality to frighten things—not like virtue broad and people cherishing.
translations.idiomatic: terror wins less than breadth of virtue that draws the people.

sentences.zh: 匹夫猶不可以力服，而況一國乎？

translations.literal: A common man still cannot be subdued by force—how much more one whole state?
translations.idiomatic: Force cannot humble even one stubborn commoner—how much less a realm?

sentences.zh: 力服猶不如以德來，而況不制乎？

translations.literal: Force-subduing still is not as good as drawing them by virtue—how much more when not controlled?
translations.idiomatic: Coercion ranks below attraction by virtue—especially when you lack control.

sentences.zh: 是以羊祜恢大同之略，思五兵之則，齊其民人，均其施澤，振義網以羅強吳，明兼愛以革暴俗，易生民之視聽，馳不戰乎江表。

translations.literal: Therefore Yang Hu expanded the grand unity strategy, pondered the five weapons' norms, aligned his people, equalized his extending kindness, shook the net of righteousness to net strong Wu, clarified inclusive love to reform violent custom, changed living people's seeing and hearing—galloping without battle east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yang Hu pursued universal harmony, balanced arms with mercy, evened his kindness across Wu, spread inclusive love to tame brutality, and reshaped hearts south of the river without drawing swords.

sentences.zh: 故能德音悅暢，而襁負雲集，殊鄰異域，義讓交弘，自吳之遇敵，未有若此者也。

translations.literal: Therefore able to make virtuous sounds joyful and smooth—while infants on backs cloud-gather; distant neighbors different regions—righteous yielding mutually vast—since Wu met enemies, never has there been like this.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation drew crowds across borders; never had Wu faced so benign an adversary.

sentences.zh: 抗見國小主暴，而晉德彌昌，人積兼己之善，而己無固本之規，百姓懷嚴敵之德，闔境有棄主之慮，思所以鎮定民心，緝寧外內，奮其危弱，抗權上國者，莫若親行斯道，以侔其勝。

translations.literal: Kang saw the state small and lord cruel, yet Jin virtue ever flourishing; others piled accumulating surpassing self's goodness, yet self lacked rules for securing root; hundred surnames cherished stern enemy's virtue; whole border had abandon-lord worries—thinking how thereby to tranquilly settle people's hearts, harmonize quiet outer and inner, rouse its peril and weakness, oppose power upper state—nothing compares to personally practicing this Way to match its victory.
translations.idiomatic: Kang saw Wu small under a tyrant while Jin flourished; his people admired the enemy's virtue and feared abandonment. To steady hearts and brace a weak state against a great power, nothing matched answering virtue with virtue.

sentences.zh: 使彼德靡加吾，而此善流聞，歸重邦國，弘明遠風，折衝於枕席之上，校勝於帷幄之內，傾敵而不以甲兵之力，保國而不浚溝池之固，信義感於寇仇，丹懷體於先日。

translations.literal: Cause their virtue not to overspread us, while this goodness flows heard—return weight to state-guo; enlarge and clarify far winds—break clash on pillow and mat above; compare victory within tent curtain within—overthrow enemy yet not by armor and weapon's force; preserve state yet not by deepening moat and pool's solidity—faith and righteousness move robber foes; crimson heart embodies prior days.
translations.idiomatic: Let Jin's kindness fail to overshadow ours while Wu's decency travels abroad; win contests of council and conviction without bronze blades; hold the realm without relying on walls; let faith move even sworn foes and candor echo ancient honor.

sentences.zh: 豈設狙詐以危賢，徇己身之私名，貪外物之重我，闇服之而不備者哉！

translations.literal: How could one set monkey tricks to endanger worthies, follow private fame for self body, greed outer things' weighing me, blindly submit yet not prepare!
translations.idiomatic: Surely that beats petty traps that ruin good men, vanity, greed, or nodding submission without readiness!

sentences.zh: 由是論之，苟守局而保疆，一卒之所能；

translations.literal: From this discussing it—if only guarding positions and protecting borders—one soldier's ability;
translations.idiomatic: Clinging to posts is work any soldier can do;

sentences.zh: 協數以相危，小人之近事；

translations.literal: harmonizing stratagems mutually to endanger—petty men's near affairs;
translations.idiomatic: petty stratagems suit petty minds;

sentences.zh: 積詐以防物，臧獲之餘慮；

translations.literal: accumulating deceit to guard things—slaves' leftover worries;
translations.idiomatic: layered deceit is slave-level thinking;

sentences.zh: 威勝以求安，明哲之所賤。

translations.literal: awe victory to seek peace—what wise clarity despises.
translations.idiomatic: terror masquerading as peace earns contempt from the wise.

sentences.zh: 賢人君子所以拯世垂範，捨此而取彼者，其道良弘故也。〉

translations.literal: The reason worthy men and gentlemen thereby rescue the age and hang forth models—discard this and take that—their Way is truly vast therefore.
translations.idiomatic: Great men redeem ages by choosing magnanimity over meanness—that is the wider Way."

sentences.zh: 加拜都護。

translations.literal: Additionally appointed Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: He was further named Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 聞武昌左部督薛瑩征下獄。

translations.literal: He heard that Xue Ying, Left Commander of Wuchang, was summoned and cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Xue Ying of Wuchang had been jailed,

sentences.zh: 抗上疏曰：

translations.literal: Kang submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: he memorialized:

sentences.zh: 夫俊乂者，國家之良寶，社稷之貴資。

translations.literal: As for outstanding men—they are the state's fine treasures and the altars' precious assets.
translations.idiomatic: Talented ministers are the dynasty's treasure and the state's capital.

sentences.zh: 庶政所以倫敘，四門所以穆清也。

translations.literal: By them various governance achieves ordered sequence; by them the four gates achieve solemn purity.
translations.idiomatic: They bring order to policy and calm to the court.

sentences.zh: 故大司農樓玄、散騎中常侍王蕃、少府李勖，皆當世秀穎，一時顯器，既蒙初寵，從容列位，而並旋受誅殛，或圮族替祀，或投棄荒裔。

translations.literal: Therefore Grand Minister of Agriculture Lou Xuan, Cavalry Regular Attendant Wang Fan, and Chamberlain for the Palace Treasury Li Xu—all were this age's outstanding brilliance, momentary eminent vessels—having received initial favor, calmly took ranked positions—yet together soon suffered execution and extinction, some ruined clan and replaced sacrifice, some cast away to wild borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Xuan, Wang Fan, and Li Xu were pillars of their generation—honored, then executed or exiled and their lines destroyed.

sentences.zh: 蓋《周禮》有赦賢之辟，《春秋》有宥善之義。

translations.literal: For the Rites of Zhou has pardon-worthy statutes for worthies; Spring and Autumn has sparing-good meanings.
translations.idiomatic: The classics urge sparing able men.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：‘與其殺不辜，寧失不經。

translations.literal: The Documents states: 'Rather than kill the guiltless, better miss irregularity.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: "Better misjudge than execute the innocent."

sentences.zh: ’而蕃等罪名未定，大辟以加，心經忠義，身被極刑，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: ' Yet Fan and others' crimes were not yet determined—capital punishment was applied; hearts threaded loyalty and righteousness; bodies suffered utmost punishments—how not painful!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Fan and company died before verdict—loyal hearts condemned to death: unbearable!

sentences.zh: 且已死之刑，固無所識，至乃焚爍流漂，棄之水濱，懼非先王之正典，或甫侯之所戒也。

translations.literal: Moreover punishment already death—solidly nothing more to know—reaching to burning bright drift floating, cast aside at water's edge—I fear it is not former kings' proper canons—perhaps what Fu Hou warned against.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses burned or floated downstream stray from ancient statute—the caution Bo Yi warned of.

sentences.zh: 是以百姓哀聳，士民同戚。

translations.literal: Therefore hundred surnames mourn startled; scholar-officers and people share sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The people tremble; gentry and commons grieve alike.

sentences.zh: 蕃、勖永已，悔亦靡及，誠望陛下赦召玄出，而頃聞薛瑩卒見逮錄。

translations.literal: Fan and Xu forever ended—regret also never reaches—I sincerely hope Your Majesty pardons and summons Xuan out—yet recently I hear Xue Ying suddenly seen seized and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to pardon Lou Xuan; now I learn Xue Ying has also been arrested.

sentences.zh: 瑩父綜納言先帝，傅弼文皇，及瑩承基，內厲名行，今之所坐，罪在可宥。

translations.literal: Ying's father Zong was intake-speech for the late emperor, aided and assisted the civil emperor; when Ying inherited foundation, inwardly he cultivated name and conduct—what he now sits for—crime lies in what may be spared.
translations.idiomatic: His father served two sovereigns with honor; Xue Ying upheld the family name—the alleged offense deserves mercy.

sentences.zh: 臣懼有司未詳其事，如復誅戮，益失民望，乞垂天恩，原赦瑩罪，哀矜庶獄，清澄刑網，則天下幸甚！

translations.literal: Your subject fears those in charge have not detailed the matter—if again executing and slaughtering—will further lose people's hope—I beg let heavenly grace descend—originally pardon Ying's crime—pity common prisons—clarify and purify punishment's net—then under heaven extremely fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: If authorities rush execution without proof, hope dies—pardon Xue Ying, review common cases, clean the courts—the realm will rejoice!

sentences.zh: 時師旅仍動，百姓疲弊。

translations.literal: At that time armies repeatedly moved; hundred surnames were weary and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign followed campaign while the people collapsed.

sentences.zh: 抗上疏曰：

translations.literal: Kang submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang wrote:

sentences.zh: 臣聞《易》貴隨時，《傳》美觀釁，故有夏多罪而殷湯用師，紂作淫虐而周武授鉞。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard the Changes esteems following the times; the Commentary praises viewing openings—therefore Xia had many crimes and Yin Tang employed armies; Zhou practiced licentious cruelty and Zhou Wu received the axe.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes honors timely action; the Commentary praises striking when heaven shows an opening—Tang punished Xia, Wu punished Zhou.

sentences.zh: 苟無其時，玉台有憂傷之慮，孟津有反旆之軍。

translations.literal: If lacking its time—jade terrace has sorrowful worry—Meng Ford has returning-banner armies.
translations.idiomatic: Without timing, even sacred councils hesitate and armies turn back at Meng Ford.

sentences.zh: 今不務富國強兵，力農畜谷，使文武之才效展其用，百揆之署無曠厥職。

translations.literal: Now not attending to enriching state and strengthening army, striving at farming and storing grain—making civil and martial talents display and extend their use—hundred affairs' offices without vacant their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Instead of enriching the state, farming, deploying talent, and filling every office,

sentences.zh: 明黜陟以厲庶尹，審刑賞以示勸沮，訓諸司以德。

translations.literal: clarify demotions and promotions to encourage multitude of directors—carefully examine punishments and rewards to show encouragement and deterrence—instruct various offices with virtue.
translations.idiomatic: ranking officials honestly, judging rewards and punishments, teaching departments virtue,

sentences.zh: 而撫百姓以仁，然後順天乘運，席捲宇內，而聽諸將徇名，窮兵黷武，動費萬計，士卒彫瘁，寇不為衰，而我已大病矣！

translations.literal: and soothe hundred surnames with benevolence—afterward follow heaven riding fate—roll up mat within the cosmos—yet listening to various generals chase fame—exhaust armies revel in war—movement expenses ten thousand counted—soldiers withered and wasted—bandits do not thereby decline—yet we already greatly sick!
translations.idiomatic: and ruling with kindness—you indulge generals who raid for glory, waste treasure, exhaust troops, barely scratch the enemy, and leave Wu dying!

sentences.zh: 今爭帝王之資，而昧十百之利，此人臣之奸便，非國家之良策也。

translations.literal: Now contesting emperors-and-kings' capital—yet blind to ten-and-hundredfold profit—this is ministers' crafty convenience—not the state's good strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Trading imperial stature for petty gains serves plotting ministers, not Wu.

sentences.zh: 昔齊、魯三戰，魯人再克而亡不旋踵。

translations.literal: Formerly Qi and Lu three battles—Lu men twice conquered yet perished without turning heel.
translations.idiomatic: Lu twice beat Qi yet fell overnight—size decides survival.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 大小之勢異也。

translations.literal: Large and small's momentum differs.
translations.idiomatic: Power differs with scale.

sentences.zh: 況今師所克獲，不補所喪哉？

translations.literal: Moreover now what armies conquer and capture does not repay what is lost!
translations.idiomatic: Our raids hardly repay their cost!

sentences.zh: 且阻兵無眾，古之明鑒，誠宜暫息進取小規，以畜士民之力，觀釁伺隙，庶無悔吝。

translations.literal: Moreover relying on arms without masses—ancients' bright mirror—truly fitting temporarily rest advancing-taking petty schemes—to store scholar-officers and people's strength—watch openings spy gaps—perhaps without regret and stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: History warns against armies without popular backing—pause petty offensives, rebuild strength, watch for heaven's opening, avoid regret.

sentences.zh: 二年春，就拜大司馬、荊州牧。

translations.literal: Second year spring—thereupon appointed Grand Marshal and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second year he took office as Grand Marshal and Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，疾病。

translations.literal: Third year summer—illness.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：

translations.literal: Submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized:

sentences.zh: 西陵、建平，國之蕃表，既處下流，受敵二境。

translations.literal: Xiling and Jianping—the state's fence outer-markers—already situated downstream—receive enemy two borders.
translations.idiomatic: Xiling and Jianping shield the realm yet sit downstream and face two fronts.

sentences.zh: 若敵泛舟順流，舳艫千里，星奔電邁，俄然行至，非可恃援他部以救倒縣也。

translations.literal: If enemy floats boats down current—stern-to-stern a thousand li—star gallop lightning stride—instantly arrive travel—cannot rely on aiding other divisions to rescue inverted county.
translations.idiomatic: If Jin sails downstream with a thousand li of hulls, relief from elsewhere cannot arrive in time—it is an inverted county hanging by a thread.

sentences.zh: 此乃社稷安危之機，非徒封疆侵陵小害也。

translations.literal: This is the altars' safety and peril's pivot—not merely sealed borders invasion minor harm.
translations.idiomatic: This governs the fate of the altars—not a petty border scrape.

sentences.zh: 臣父遜昔在西垂陳言，以為西陵國之西門，雖雲易守，亦復易失。

translations.literal: Your subject's father Xun formerly at western edge stated opinion—holding Xiling the state's western gate—although called easy to guard—also again easy to lose.
translations.idiomatic: My father once warned that Xiling is Wu's western gate—easy to defend yet easy to lose.

sentences.zh: 若有不守，非但失一郡，則荊州非吳有也。

translations.literal: If there is failure to guard—not merely losing one commandery—then Jingzhou is not Wu's possession.
translations.idiomatic: If it falls we lose not one commandery but all Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 如其有虞，當傾國爭之。

translations.literal: If there is peril therein—ought to tilt whole state to contest it.
translations.idiomatic: At the first alarm Wu must stake everything on its defense.

sentences.zh: 臣往在西陵，得涉遜跡，前乞精兵三萬，而

translations.literal: Your subject formerly was at Xiling—was able to tread Xun's tracks—before begged crack troops thirty thousand—yet
translations.idiomatic: When I stood at Xiling in my father's footsteps I asked for thirty thousand veterans, yet

translations.literal: (to)
translations.idiomatic: (text breaks)

sentences.zh: 者循常，未肯差赴。

translations.literal: those followed routine—not willing to dispatch go.
translations.idiomatic: the clerks stuck to routine and refused to send them.

sentences.zh: 自步闡以後，益更損耗。

translations.literal: From Bu Chan onward, losses grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: After the Bu Chan affair our strength shrank further.

sentences.zh: 今臣所統千里，受敵四處，外御強對，內懷百蠻，而上下見兵財有數萬，羸弊日久，難以待變。

translations.literal: Now what your subject commands is a thousand li, receiving enemies on four sides; outwardly resisting strong foes, inwardly cherishing hundred barbarians—yet above and below visible troops amount to only several tens of thousands; exhausted and worn long—hard to await change.
translations.idiomatic: I hold a thousand li against enemies on four fronts—foreign foes without, tribes within—yet fewer than ten thousand fit soldiers remain after years of strain; I cannot meet a crisis.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為諸王幼沖，未統國事，可且立傅相，輔導賢姿，無用兵馬，以妨要務。

translations.literal: Your foolish subject believes the various kings are young and tender, have not yet unified state affairs—may for the moment establish tutors and chancellors, instruct and guide worthy talents—do not employ horses and troops so as to obstruct urgent tasks.
translations.idiomatic: The royal princes are minors—appoint tutors instead of drafting their households for war and distracting vital business.

sentences.zh: 又黃門豎宦，開立占募，兵民怨役，逋逃入占。

translations.literal: Moreover Yellow Gate eunuchs opened standing recruitment—soldiers and commoners resent labor—fugitives flee into recruitment rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs monopolize recruitment; troops and peasants resent corvée and flee into their nets.

sentences.zh: 乞特詔簡閱，一切料出，以補疆場受敵常處，使臣所部足滿八萬，省息眾務，信其賞罰，雖韓、白復生，無所展巧。

translations.literal: I beg special edict for inspection and review—everything measured out—to replenish the border fields that constantly receive enemy—cause your subject's command to reach full eighty thousand—reduce and rest various affairs—trust in their rewards and punishments—even if Han Xin and Bai Qi came again to life—nowhere to display craft.
translations.idiomatic: Issue an edict to audit every draft and redeploy those men to the threatened sectors until my command reaches eighty thousand. Cut wasteful duties and enforce clear rewards—even Han Xin and Bai Qi could do no better.

sentences.zh: 若兵不增，此制不改，而欲克諧大事，此臣之所深戚也。

translations.literal: If troops are not increased, this system not altered—yet wishing to succeed and harmonize great affairs—this is what your subject deeply sorrows over.
translations.idiomatic: Without more troops and reform, hoping for great success is what I dread most.

sentences.zh: 若臣死之後，乞以西方為屬。

translations.literal: If after your subject's death—I beg to take the west as entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, treat the western frontier as the realm's first charge.

sentences.zh: 願陛下思覽臣言，則臣死且不朽。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty think and view your subject's words—then your subject dies yet not decaying.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty weighs these words, I may die without regret.

sentences.zh: 秋遂卒，子晏嗣。

translations.literal: In autumn he then died; his son Yan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died that autumn; his son Lu Yan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 晏及弟景、玄、機、雲、分領抗兵。

translations.literal: Yan together with younger brothers Jing, Xuan, Ji, and Yun divided leading Kang's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and his brothers Jing, Xuan, Ji, and Yun split their father's command.

sentences.zh: 晏為裨將軍、夷道監。

translations.literal: Yan was Lieutenant-General and supervisor of Yidao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan became Lieutenant-General and inspector of Yidao.

sentences.zh: 天紀四年，晉軍伐吳，龍驤將軍王浚順流東下。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianji, Jin armies campaigned against Wu; General Who Spreads Dragons Wang Jun went downstream east.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianji 4 (280 CE) Jin invaded Wu; Wang Jun sailed downriver.

sentences.zh: 所至輒克，終如抗慮。

translations.literal: Wherever they arrived they at once prevailed—in the end as Kang had feared.
translations.idiomatic: City after city fell—exactly as Lu Kang had warned.

sentences.zh: 景字士仁，以尚公主拜騎都尉，封毗陵侯，既領抗兵，拜偏將軍、中夏督，澡身好學，著書數十篇也。

translations.literal: Jing, courtesy name Shiren—by marrying the princess was appointed Commandant of Cavalry, enfeoffed Marquis of Piling—having taken over Kang's troops, appointed Lieutenant-General and commander of Zhongxia—bathed body and loved learning—authored several tens of treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jing, styled Shiren, married a princess and became Commandant of Cavalry and Marquis of Piling; commanding his father's troops he rose to Lieutenant-General and Zhongxia commander, lived cleanly, studied widely, and wrote dozens of essays.

sentences.zh: 〈《文士传》曰：陆景母张承女，诸葛恪外生。

translations.literal: The Literary Men's Tradition states: Lu Jing's mother was Zhang Cheng's daughter—Zhuge Ke's sister—thus Lu Jing was Zhuge Ke's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: The Literary Men's Tradition says Lu Jing's mother was Zhang Cheng's daughter and Zhuge Ke's sister—Lu Jing was Zhuge Ke's nephew.

sentences.zh: 恪诛，景母坐见黜。

translations.literal: When Ke was executed, Jing's mother sat guilty and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Ke fell, she lost her rank.

sentences.zh: 景少为祖母所育养，及祖母亡，景为之心丧三年。〉

translations.literal: Jing in youth was foster-nurtured by grandmother; when grandmother died, Jing for her observed heart-mourning three years.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother raised him; when she died he mourned her three years though not bound by ritual."

sentences.zh: 二月壬戌，晏為王浚別軍所殺。

translations.literal: Second month renxu—Yan was killed by Wang Jun's detached army.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu in the second month Yan fell to Wang Jun's flank force.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，景亦遇害，時年三十一。

translations.literal: Guihai—Jing also suffered violence; at the time age thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jing died as well, aged thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 景妻，孫皓適妹，與景俱張承外孫也。

translations.literal: Jing's wife was Sun Hao's legitimate younger sister—with Jing both were Zhang Cheng's maternal grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's wife was Sun Hao's full sister; both were Zhang Cheng's grandchildren.

sentences.zh: 〈景弟机，字士衡，云字士龙。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Ji, courtesy name Shiheng; Yun courtesy name Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brothers Lu Ji, styled Shiheng, and Lu Yun, styled Shilong:

sentences.zh: 《机云别传》曰：晋太康末，俱入洛，造司空张华，华一见而奇之，曰：「伐吴之役，利在获二俊。

translations.literal: The Separate Biography of Ji and Yun states: Late Taikang of Jin, both entered Luoyang—visited Minister of Works Zhang Hua—Hua on one seeing wondered at them, saying: "The Wu campaign's profit lies in obtaining two talents.
translations.idiomatic: Their biography says that in late Taikang they called on Zhang Hua in Luoyang; he exclaimed that conquering Wu's real prize was capturing these two men.

sentences.zh: 」遂为之延誉，荐之诸公。

translations.literal: " Thereupon for them extended praise—recommended them to various nobles.
translations.idiomatic: He praised them everywhere and recommended them at court.

sentences.zh: 太傅杨骏辟机为祭酒，转太子洗马、尚书著作郎。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yang Jun summoned Ji as libationer—transferred crown prince horse-washer, Secretariat drafting gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun named Ji libationer; he later served as crown prince attendant and Secretariat compiler.

sentences.zh: 云为吴王郎中令，出宰浚仪，甚有惠政，吏民怀之，生为立祠。

translations.literal: Yun was Prince of Wu's palace attendant chief—went out to administer Junyi—had very generous governance—clerks and people cherished him—in life they erected shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was steward to the Prince of Wu, then magistrate of Junyi, where his kindness earned shrines while he still lived.

sentences.zh: 后并历显位。

translations.literal: Later both passed through eminent positions.
translations.idiomatic: Both rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 机天才绮练，文藻之美，独冠於时。

translations.literal: Ji's heaven-bestowed talent was lustrously refined—literary ornament's beauty—alone crowned the age.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's genius and prose stood unrivaled.

sentences.zh: 云亦善属文，清新不及机，而口辩持论过之。

translations.literal: Yun also was good at composing texts—fresh clarity did not match Ji—but mouth debate holding discourse surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun wrote well—less brilliant than his brother but sharper in debate.

sentences.zh: 于时朝廷多故，机、云并自结於成都王颖。

translations.literal: At that time court had many troubles—Ji and Yun both personally tied themselves to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When the court convulsed, both brothers attached themselves to Sima Ying.

sentences.zh: 颖用机为平原相，云清河内史。

translations.literal: Ying employed Ji as Pingyuan administrator—Yun as Qinghe interior historian.
translations.idiomatic: Ying made Ji governor of Pingyuan and Yun administrator of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 寻转云右司马，甚见委仗。

translations.literal: Soon transferred Yun to Right Majordomo—greatly seen entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Yun soon became right majordomo and enjoyed Ying's full trust.

sentences.zh: 无几而与长沙王构隙，遂举兵攻洛，以机行后将军，督王粹、牵秀等诸军二十万，士龙著南征赋以美其事。

translations.literal: Before long formed rift with Prince of Changsha—thereupon raised armies attacking Luoyang—made Ji acting Rear General—supervised Wang Cui, Qian Xiu and others various armies two hundred thousand—Shilong composed Southern Campaign Rhapsody to praise the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ying quarreled with the Prince of Changsha and marched on Luoyang with two hundred thousand men under Ji, Wang Cui, and Qian Xiu; Lu Yun composed the Southern Campaign Rhapsody to glorify it.

sentences.zh: 机吴人，羁旅单宦，顿居群士之右，多不厌服。

translations.literal: Ji was a Wu man—lodging-travel solitary official—suddenly dwelt above host of gentlemen—many were not satisfied and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: A lone Wu outsider thrust above northern officers—many resented him.

sentences.zh: 机屡战失利，死散过半。

translations.literal: Ji repeatedly battled and lost advantage—dead and scattered exceeded half.
translations.idiomatic: Ji lost battle after battle; more than half his men fled or died.

sentences.zh: 初，宦人孟玖，颖所嬖幸，乘宠豫权，云数言其短，颖不能纳，玖又从而毁之。

translations.literal: At first eunuch Meng Jiu—whom Ying favored—rode favor to preempt power—Yun repeatedly spoke his shortcomings—Ying could not accept—Jiu moreover followed and slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: The favorite eunuch Meng Jiu abused his influence; Lu Yun exposed him but Ying ignored the warnings and Jiu slandered Yun.

sentences.zh: 是役也，玖弟超亦领众配机，不奉军令。

translations.literal: In this campaign Jiu's younger brother Chao also led masses assigned to Ji—did not obey military orders.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chao served under Ji but ignored orders.

sentences.zh: 机绳之以法，超宣言曰陆机将反。

translations.literal: Ji bound him by law—Chao publicly declared saying Lu Ji will rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Ji disciplined him; Chao cried treason.

sentences.zh: 及牵秀等谮机於颖，以为持两端，玖又构之於内，颖信之，遣收机，并收云及弟耽，并伏法。

translations.literal: When Qian Xiu and others slandered Ji to Ying—thought him holding two ends—Jiu moreover framed him within—Ying believed—sent to seize Ji—and seized Yun together with younger brother Dan—all suffered law.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiu accused Ji of playing both sides; Meng Jiu whispered in court; Ying believed him and arrested Ji, Yun, and their brother Dan—all were executed.

sentences.zh: 机兄弟既江南之秀，亦著名诸夏，并以无罪夷灭，天下痛惜之。

translations.literal: Ji brothers were already Jiangnan's excellence—also famed north of rivers—and together without guilt were extirpated—world grieved and pitied them.
translations.idiomatic: The luminaries of the south perished innocent—the realm mourned.

sentences.zh: 机文章为世所重，云所著亦传於世。

translations.literal: Ji's writings were esteemed by the age—what Yun authored also transmitted in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's prose became canonical; Lu Yun's survives as well.

sentences.zh: 初，抗之克步阐也，诛及婴孩，识道者尤之曰：「后世必受其殃！

translations.literal: At first when Kang conquered Bu Chan—execution reached infants—those who knew the Way blamed him saying: "Later generations surely will suffer its calamity!
translations.idiomatic: When Kang slaughtered Bu Chan's line down to infants, wise men said: "His house will answer for it!

sentences.zh: 」及机之诛，三族无遗，孙惠与硃诞书曰：「马援择君，凡人所闻，不意三陆相携暴朝，杀身伤名，可为悼叹。

translations.literal: " When Ji's execution came—three clans none remained—Sun Hui wrote to Zhu Dan saying: "Ma Yuan chose lords—ordinary men have heard—did not expect three Lu together dragging violent court—kill body harm name—may be mourned and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lu clan perished root and branch, Sun Hui wrote Zhu Dan: "Ma Yuan chose his lord wisely—we never thought the three Lu would cling to a tyrant court and lose life and fame—heartbreaking.

sentences.zh: 」事亦并在晋书。〉

translations.literal: " The affairs also together are in Jin History.
translations.idiomatic: The tale fills the Jinshu."

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：「劉備天下稱雄，一世所憚，陸遜春秋方壯，威名未著，摧而克之，罔不如志。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: "Liu Bei was acclaimed hero under heaven—what the age feared—Lu Xun's spring-and-autumn was just robust—awe-name not yet manifest—shattered and conquered him—none did not accord with intent.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: "Liu Bei terrified his age, yet the young Lu Xun—still unknown—crushed him utterly.

sentences.zh: 予既奇遜之謀略，又歎權之識才，所以濟大事也。

translations.literal: I both marvel at Xun's stratagem and tactics—and sigh at Quan's recognizing talent—thereby completing great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I admire Xun's strategy and Sun Quan's eye for talent—the partnership that won Wu's great battles.

sentences.zh: 及遜忠誠懇至，憂國亡身，庶幾社稷之臣矣。

translations.literal: And Xun's loyalty sincere and earnest—worrying state till body perished—perhaps nearly altars' minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xun served with utter loyalty until grief consumed him—a true pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 抗貞亮籌干，咸有父風，奕世載美，具體而微，可謂克構者哉!」

translations.literal: Kang's steadfast brightness planning stem—all had father's wind—successive generations bear beauty—having body yet small—may be called able to complete structure!"
translations.idiomatic: Kang matched his father's steadfast genius across generations—compressed yet complete; he indeed upheld the house."
